Manage Operations & Resources: Build and manage operational plans, budgets, and external vendor or production partner relationships, balancing ambitious creative output with smart resource allocation.
Minimum qualifications: 10+ years of experience leading content strategy, creative production, or digital media programming at scale, spanning both product or sales enablement content and culture or employer brand storytelling, including 5+ years of people management experience building and leading creative or content teams.
Demonstrated expertise in short-form, platform-native video and mobile-first content formats designed to drive organic user engagement and retention.
Proven track record of hands-on creative direction, with the ability to evaluate and guide scripts, storyboards, and video edits from concept through final delivery.
Experience using audience analytics and engagement metrics to run test-and-learn cycles, optimize content roadmaps, and manage catalog lifecycle.
Experience managing production budgets, external agencies or production partners, and end-to-end production workflows.
Experience scaling content globally across multiple markets, languages, and cultural contexts.
Preferred qualifications: Experience managing multidisciplinary teams that include instructional designers or learning experience specialists alongside video producers and writers.
Deep familiarity with AI-accelerated content production and localization workflows, with a clear point of view on balancing speed and scale with creative quality.
Experience working in an embedded model with Product Management on mobile app experiences, conversational Q&A, or search-driven content delivery.
Track record of briefing, influencing, and aligning senior cross-functional executives across global and regional teams.
Background in global retail, channel sales enablement, consumer technology, or creator-economy media platforms.

title: Health Sensing HW - Module Design Engineer
description:
The Health Sensing Hardware team is looking for a highly-motivated optical engineer to work on the next-generation of optical health sensors.
The successful candidate will be able to leverage training in optical system design, modeling and fabrication to develop the optical health sensors in the Apple Watch and AirPods. This candidate should also be adept at analyzing user data to infer real-world performance trends and emergent behavior. Lastly, the candidate must be able to distill simulation and empirical results into concise design assessments to cross-functional collaborators and senior management.
You will be working with a team of research scientists and hardware engineers developing technologies for the optical health sensors. You will be responsible for the optical design of the sensor via simulations and prototype-based assessments, user studies and analysis of sensor performance. The role also requires strong data analysis skills to infer trends and dependencies in the data to improve the understanding of skin-sensor interactions and directly impact the design and performance of the health sensors. This is a highly cross-functional role and will require close collaboration with mechanical, electrical and software engineers. Lastly, you will be responsible for delivering detailed assessments and designs evaluations to leadership and cross-functional partners.
Minimum qualifications: Knowledge of optical system design for wearable sensing applications including lens design, integration of electro-optical components etc.
Experience with building bench-top optical sensor prototypes including metrology and characterization.
Experience working with cross-functional teams (mechanical/electrical engineering) on technology development of optical sensors.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, excellent documentation skills.
BS with 3+ years industry experience or MS/PhD in Biomedical Engineering, Optical Engineering, or related field.

Experience with modeling/simulating light transport in biological tissue.
Proven experience in designing optical systems for bio-sensing/imaging applications.
PhD in Biomedical or Optical Engineering.

title: InfoSec Development Program (ISDP), Full-Time Opportunities
description:
The Apple Information Security (AIS) team is responsible for developing services to find and mitigate security risks faced by Apple. We are seeking extraordinary engineers with multi-faceted skills in software development, networking, data science and computing infrastructure to create tools, services, and frameworks critical to this charter.
Apple's InfoSec Development Program (ISDP) is a two year rotational program that offers a completely customizable series of assignments. Upon completion of the program, you will use your experiences in advanced roles across the organization. The program provides opportunities for hands on learning with a variety of teams in a rapidly growing and dynamic setting. You will have the opportunity to meet with Information Security Leaders as well as build community amongst your peers by attending educational and social events.

Related software engineering internship or job experience
Strong software design, problem solving and debugging skills

Passion for high-quality code, tests, CI/CD, documentation, and production services
Act with high ethical standards and integrity

title: Inventory Operations Specialist, Data Center Operations
description:
Do you want to help build some of the largest and most consequential enterprise and customer technology systems in the world? Join Apple’s Information Systems and Technology (IS&T) organization. IS&T is the engine behind everything Apple does for customers and for the people who build for them. It’s Apple’s central nervous system. Supporting 2.5 billion active Apple devices, processing billions of secure transactions, and keeping the technology that defines modern life running flawlessly, IS&T makes the impossible feel effortless.
Do you love building solutions to handle global complexity and immense scale? Imagine what you could do here.

Ability to lift up to 50 pounds waist high.
Valid Driver's License.

title: MAC Design Verification Engineer
description:

Proficient in shell and Python scripting, Perl scripting.

Should be a team player with excellent communication skills, self-motivated and well organized.

Active personal interest in AI agents—you're already experimenting on your own time.

title: Machine Learning Engineer, Agentic AI- Worldwide Product Marketing
description:
As a Machine Learning Engineer, you will design and build AI/ML systems — from classical predictive models to LLM-powered agentic applications — that drive meaningful business outcomes at scale. You will take solutions from research and experimentation through to robust, production-grade deployment, with a growing focus on autonomous agents that reason, plan, use tools, and act on behalf of users and business processes. Proficiency in Python with hands-on experience building distributed systems
Experience building large-scale machine learning systems using big data technologies such as Spark, SQL, Snowflake, or similar platforms

title: Machine Learning Engineer, Answers Knowledge and Information - Proactive
description:
The Information Intelligence team is creating groundbreaking technology for artificial intelligence, machine learning and natural language processing! The features we create are redefining how hundreds of millions of people use their computers and mobile devices to search and find what they are looking for. Our universal search engine powers search features across a variety of Apple products, including Siri, Spotlight, Safari, Messages and Lookup. We also develop state-of-the-art generative AI technologies based on Large Language Models to power innovative features in both Apple’s devices and services on the cloud. As part of this group, you will be doing large scale machine learning and deep learning research and development to improve Open Domain Question Answering (using both structured knowledge graph data and unstructured web data) and Summarization as well as developing fundamental building blocks needed for Artificial Intelligence. Experience working with Python and at least one of the deep learning frameworks such as TensorFlow, PyTorch, or JAX

At least 2 years of experience in various state-of-the-art techniques related to LLM fine-tuning in 1 or more of the following areas -- Supervised Fine-tuning (SFT) with Rejection Sampling, Preference-based fine-tuning techniques (e.g RLHF, Reward model, DPO, PPO, GRPO etc.), Parameter efficient fine-tuning techniques (e.g LoRA), Hallucination reduction and factual accuracy improvements, Designing and implementing safety guardrails

title: Machine Learning Engineer, Computer Vision

title: Machine Learning Systems Engineer – Video Computer Vision

title: RF System Integration Engineer (Instrument Engineering)

description:

Experienced in Cadence Virtuoso, Spectre RF, Matlab, EM simulation (EMX, HFSS), and similar tools.

description:

It is driven by a world-class, vertically integrated team spanning RF/Analog, Systems/PHY/MAC, VLSI/RTL design and integration, Emulation, Design Verification, Test and Validation, and FW/SW engineering. As a Wireless SOC Design Verification Engineer, you’ll be at the heart of the chip design effort — owning a meaningful verification scope and growing it project to project.
You’ll be responsible for pre-silicon RTL verification at the block, subsystem, and top-level SOC, taking your scope from test planning through coverage closure and signoff. Working closely with architects, designers, and firmware engineers, you’ll build reusable testbenches and verification environments using modern, metric-driven methodology. Areas you may work on include the Power Management Unit, CPU subsystem, DMA, on-chip debug infrastructure, PCIe, bus fabric, boot and secure-boot sequencing, MAC-PHY Verification, Radio integration, and peripherals such as SPI — choosing simulation, formal, or whichever approach the design actually calls for. Low power is part of your scope wherever it shows up: you’ll verify power intent using UPF within your area.
Over time, you can grow deeper into the IPs and subsystems you know best, or broader — across IPs and up from block level to full SOC integration. The team is also pushing hard on AI-assisted verification, and you’ll help figure out where it fits best: test generation, debug, coverage closure, or all the above.

Hands-on experience across the verification cycle: test planning, testbench implementation, test creation and debug, and coverage closure.
Strong SystemVerilog and Verilog skills, with solid working knowledge of UVM.
Solid problem-solving and debugging skills with constrained-random verification.
Understanding of digital logic design, SOC architecture, and microarchitecture.

Verification experience with PCIe, bus fabric/NOC, or AHB/AXI-based architectures in a UVM environment.
Experience verifying IP or top-level integration for a WiFi or Bluetooth SOC, or knowledge of wireless protocols.
Experience with low-power verification, UPF, boot-up, power-cycling, and HW/FW interaction.

You will build the pipelines and table designs that power forecasting, capacity planning, and fair cross-charging across the organization, and help us spot issues before an internal customer ever notices them. Knowledge of CDR architectures and implementations
Knowledge of lab equipment and testing
Experience in Analog Mixed Signal circuit modeling and performance evaluation (e.g. SystemVerilog, Matlab, Python, VerilogAMS)

title: Technical Program Manager and Manufacturing Quality Engineer
description:
Imagine what you could do here. At Apple, new ideas have a way of becoming extraordinary products, services, and customer experiences very quickly. Bring passion and dedication to your job and there's no telling what you could accomplish. The people here at Apple don’t just create products — they create the kind of wonder that’s revolutionized entire industries. It’s the diversity of those people and their ideas that inspires the innovation that runs through everything we do, from amazing technology to industry-leading environmental efforts. Join Apple, and help us leave the world better than we found it.
In this highly visible role, you will have process (TPM) and quality engineering (MQE) responsibility for next generation Apple products. This will require you to lead selection, implementation & optimization of manufacturing processes and quality planning and deployment.
In the TPM responsibility, you will utilize your Engineering experience and work cross functionally with Product Design Engineering and Industrial Design to assess product features for manufacturability, and recommend capable processes and equipment.
In the MQE responsibility, you work in tandem with Apple's renowned designers to develop measurement & metrology technologies, quality control plans, information systems, and manufacturing methods that achieve industry-leading specifications at massive production scale. We handle a network of supplier factories worldwide, with responsibility for our partners to deliver to bold schedules. Our focus is on elegant execution of extraordinary industrial designs, resulting in products that thrill our customers.
Process Development:
Planning, proposing, and leading experiments to produce timely and accurate analyses used to drive design, development, and supply chain decisions.
Assessing the suitability of a fabrication technology for a given part design. Planning validation exercises to demonstrate initial feasibility as well as manufacturing capability. Analyzing results of validation exercises and provide technical recommendations.
Reviewing progress of development activities at supplier locations and serve as point of escalation for critical process related issues.
New Product Introduction:
Help to drive process development and capability assessment activities, reviewing part design documentation to ensure alignment with process capability.
Assigns specific tasks and work with Apple suppliers to support process development and/or data gathering activities. Set clear goals for results and provide timely reviews of performance throughout program.
Establish validation procedures to figure out acceptance of tooling into development builds as well as mass production.
Supplier Execution:
Review supplier tool design, process flow, equipment selection, DFM, and DOE proposals. Identify shortfalls and corrective actions to ensure design compliance.
Work with supplier engineering teams to map out process development exercises, secure resources, and commit to schedules in line with program goals
Assess supplier readiness to support build events and production ramp. Identify potential execution issues and provide recommendations to mitigate risk.
You will utilize your Quality Engineering background in the following areas:
Quality Planning
Apply solid understanding of quality control and manufacturing concepts to develop specific Product Quality Plan (PQP) appropriate to program and commodity.
Coordinate all Quality Engineering functions for a program, serving as project manager to lead efforts at supplier locations.
Actively participate in the program planning and monitoring process assuming responsibility for key deliverables at all milestones.
Provide technical direction and guidance to other Quality Engineers supporting the implementation of the PQP.
Assess measurability and creatively address concerns directly with stakeholders. Identify and direct studies to implement improvements in measuring method where appropriate.
Establish audit procedures appropriate to program and supplier to ensure adherence to Apple quality standards. Implement FAI and Cp/Cpk reviews of mechanical parts.
Supplier Quality Management
Assists supplier selection process for new products and second sourcing activities supporting qualification/disqualification decisions.
Review PQP with supplier and other Apple functional groups to optimize supplier quality programs. Evaluates supplier readiness and adherence to PQP at all development and qualification stages.
Monitor each supplier's performance through measurement of production line statistics, company inspections, and audits. Prepare summary of performance and communicate to appropriate management to ensure effective corrective action plans can be promptly executed.
At Apple, a Supplier Quality Engineer defines product cosmetic specifications and manufacturing quality control methods. Reviews processing techniques and methods applied in the manufacture, fabrication, and evaluation of products. Involvement may begin at any step from product concept to full-scale manufacturing. Coordinates design requirement review with appropriate engineering/scientific personnel to ensure capability of manufacturing processes. Compiles and evaluates data to determine appropriate limits and variables for process, material, and part specifications. May conceive and plan projects involving definition and selection of new concepts, product inspection technology, and approaches in the processing or development of new or improved processes. Recommends and implements equipment and process modifications to improve production efficiencies, manufacturing techniques and production yields for existing products. Develops and conducts statistical analysis such as Design of Experiments (DOE) and Statistical Process Control (SPC) targeting cause of failure for yield loss and improving quality.
Minimum qualifications: BS in Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Engineering Management.
1+ years experience supporting new product launches from a mechanical, process engineering, quality planning, quality engineering or product development perspective.
Experience developing process quality plans, supplier quality audits, and driving corrective actions and failure analysis efforts.
Knowledge of mechanical quality and reliability concepts, supplier management, and general manufacturing operations.
Requires International travel to supplier sites.
Preferred qualifications: Experience with soft materials (non-wovens, wovens, knits, leather) and inputs to those materials (yarns, raw materials) is strongly preferred. Experience with mechanical fabricated parts, or adhesives, glues, jigs, fixtures, tooling, injection molding, plastics experience may be acceptable.
International experience, particularly in Asia is a plus
Must have proven hands-on mechanical ability. Demonstrate excellent written and verbal communication skills. Domestic and International travel required. Experience with highly cosmetic parts a plus.

title: Wireless MAC Design Verification Engineer
description:

title: Wireless Module Engineer
description:
Apple is where individual imaginations gather committing to the values that lead to great work. Every new product we build, service we create, or Apple Store experience we deliver is the result of us making each other’s ideas stronger. That happens because every one of us shares a belief that we can make something wonderful and share it with the world, changing lives for the better. It’s the diversity of our people and their thinking that inspires the innovation that runs through everything we do. When we bring everybody in, we can do the best work of our lives. Here, you’ll do more than join something — you’ll add something. The Wireless Module Engineer (WME) is well-versed in multiple fields for wireless module development: RF design, packaging, product engineering (including yield analysis), ATE, and reliability engineering.
The Wireless Module Engineer (WME) is a highly motivated, self-driven technical lead responsible for driving the development of wireless modules from early architecture definition through mass-production ramp. This role requires strong cross-functional collaboration and the ability to deeply engage across a broad spectrum of technical domains including RF design, reliability, manufacturing test, supply chain, and system integration. The WME will initiate and lead early-phase RF architecture and specification discussions between internal engineering teams and Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly & Test (OSAT). They will ensure all OSATs comply with internal specification formats, review procedures, and approval workflows. The WME will drive the formal module design release process, establishing and reviewing checkpoints for schematics, PCB layout, electromagnetic/RF simulation results, design-for-manufacturability (DFM), test data readiness, and OSAT design feedback
In addition to communicating risks and priorities, the core responsibility of WME is to manage module integration and ATE test coverage at OSATs. WME will function as a general manager overseeing all aspects of ATE maturity preparation for hardware—such as load boards, daughter cards, sockets, and handlers—and software, firmware, module calibrations, GRR, and CPK/data analysis.
This role is expected to drive OSATs, set priorities, and collaborate closely with them to validate and approve the final ATE hardware and software integration, test coverage, and corresponding test limits, ensuring timely delivery of tested modules for product NPI builds. Following the NPI builds, WME will lead the failure analysis process with the OSATs and work with them to implement improvement activities, including enhancing ATE testers, optimizing software/firmware test time, and improving overall yield and retest rates. This role will involve traveling to international OSATs for Module & ATE bring up for 1-2 weeks before the product NPI builds. WME is expected to have a broad spectrum of technical depth to debug additional bring up issues during travel. For e.g. I2C & PCIe interface related issues. This team member will facilitate collaboration with multi-functional groups at Apple and define the test coverage. Typical test coverage includes but not limited to Open-Short & Continuity test, VCO calibration and test, TX/RX power calibration and test, RF packet test, EVM test, RX sensitivity test. They will collaborate closely with internal reliability engineering teams to translate expected product field-usage profiles into feasible and data-driven reliability test models for modules and components. This role supports multiple product lines within the Hardware Technology organization, ensuring technical excellence, risk visibility, and disciplined execution from early concept through manufacturing ramp.

title: Wireless SOC Design Verification Engineer
description:

As a Wireless SOC Verification Engineer, you’ll own your verification scope end-to-end — starting with a well-defined block or feature and growing in scope and complexity as you do. Over time, you’ll build depth in the IPs you know best and breadth across others, from block-level verification up toward subsystem and SOC integration.
You’ll own verification for your scope — with a mentor’s guidance as you build toward full ownership — on a chip that ships in every new iPhone, starting with a block or feature sized to where you are and expanding from there. You’ll work across the Power Management Unit, the CPU subsystem, on-chip debug infrastructure, PCIe, bus fabric, boot and secure-boot sequencing, and peripherals like SPI and UART — primarily through simulation, with exposure to formal verification as you grow. Low-power is part of the picture too: you’ll get hands-on with power intent verification using UPF within your scope. AI is reshaping how the team works, and you’ll help apply AI-assisted tools for test generation, debug, or verification closure as part of your day-to-day.

title: Global Supply Manager - Services
description:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Base is looking for a Global Supply Manager to own strategy and procurement for the services and partners that keep Base building, delivering, and scaling. The individual will be focused on facility services, HVAC and building maintenance, utilities, furniture, signage, office supplies, and food and beverage. Base is opening locations across the country, and today each site finds its own vendors from scratch. You'll replace that with nationwide agreements, a preferred vendor list, and a repeatable vendor playbook for every new site, using Base's combined volume to get better pricing and more consistent service.

While experience in facilities or procurement is valuable, we’re more interested in finding exceptional people who learn quickly, take ownership, and are excited to build. This is a chance to help build a procurement organization from the ground up, with meaningful ownership, direct work with business leaders, and hands-on experience in negotiation, commercial strategy, contract drafting, supplier management, cost optimization, and executive communication from day one.

 


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Lead end-to-end sourcing for Base warehouses, including facility services, HVAC and building maintenance, utilities, furniture, signage, office supplies, and catered food.

 - Negotiate nationwide and regional agreements that use Base's total volume to lower cost and give every site consistent pricing, service levels, and terms.

 - Build and maintain a preferred vendor list and site playbook so the internal team can get core services in place at a new location quickly, without recreating the wheel each time.

 - Draft, review, redline, and negotiate contracts with service providers, and suppliers, including master service agreements, statements of work, pricing schedules, and service-level terms, writing clear language that conveys business intent and reduces risk.

 - Run RFPs and RFQs, benchmark pricing, and recommend the right commercial structure (e.g., national vs. regional coverage, fixed vs. usage-based pricing) based on business needs and risk.

 - Partner with Workplace Operations, Deployments, Real Estate & Construction, Finance, Legal, and site leaders to understand requirements and launch timelines, working toward practical, cost-effective solutions.

 - Run regular supplier scorecard reviews on cost, service quality, and responsiveness, and give suppliers clear feedback that drives improvement.

 - Travel periodically to Base sites to understand needs, meet suppliers, and support new site launches.

 


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - High ownership and work ethic: you take responsibility for outcomes, follow through on commitments, and put in the effort to help build a world-class procurement organization.

 - Fast learner, comfortable with ambiguity: you quickly learn new categories, markets, and suppliers, and are resourceful enough to create clarity and next steps when no playbook exists.

 - Strong communicator: able to influence site leaders, operators, and suppliers without formal authority.

 - Sharp analytical and commercial instincts: strong problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple priorities with urgency.

 - Background in procurement, sourcing, facilities management, operations, finance, or consulting preferred. Experience with facility services or multi-site spend is a plus.

 


ABOUT THE TEAM

Our strategic procurement team procures the goods and services Base runs on outside of the battery itself: software, site services, facilities, equipment, consumables, contractors, and the vendor relationships behind them. We're building the function from the ground up, setting up the contracts, vendor lists, and processes that let every team buy quickly without overpaying. As Base grows, the agreements this team puts in place decide how fast we grow and our spend and savings.

Every dollar we save goes back into the mission. Homeowners across the country rely on Base for whole-home backup and below-market electricity rates, while our aggregated storage supports grid stability at a moment when demand is accelerating from AI infrastructure, electrification, and extreme weather. You'll get real ownership, direct access to business leaders, and the chance to shape how a fast-growing energy company buys.



Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.
   
   


DO THE BEST WORK OF YOUR LIFE AT BASE.

Job Description
This position assists in providing service to customers and their vehicles by disbursing and accurately recording gasoline disbursement in vehicles.
Responsibilities:
Distribute and accurately record gasoline disbursed in vehicles.
Enter fuel usage in AS400 via TC75.
Start vehicles, check fuel gages, mark vehicles that need fuel, and return to fuel them.
Operate a service truck and answering radio calls.
Report and record Auction gasoline levels and alert proper person to avoid running out of gasoline in main fill area.
Report inoperable vehicles to Supervisor or Assistant Manager.
Jump start vehicles and put air in tires if needed
Report damage or malfunctioning equipment on vehicles (i.e., pumps, fuel trucks).
Assist customers in locating vehicles.
Assist in sale day duties as needed (i.e., drive, act as lane leader, jump start vehicles, change tires, etc.).
Assist in audits of gasoline disbursement when necessary.
Visibly demonstrate safety commitment by following all safety and health procedures and modeling the behaviors related to such. Actively participate in support of all safety activities aligned with Safety Excellence.
Perform other duties as assigned by management.

Minimum
High School Diploma/GED and 3 years’ experience in a related field.

Safe drivers needed; Valid driver's license required.
Effective customer service and interpersonal skills required.
Ability to drive vehicles with standard and automatic transmission.
Basic mechanical knowledge.
Ability to work safely in a fast-paced environment.
Ability to sit for prolonged periods of time.
Ability to enter and exit vehicles frequently.
Ability to lift 1-25 pounds.
Vision abilities required include close, distance and color vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.
Regularly required to stand, walk, reach, talk and hear. Frequently required to stoop, kneel, crouch, bend, squat and climb.

description:

Compensation
Compensation includes a base salary in the range of $148,500.00 - $247,500.00. The base salary may vary within the anticipated base pay range based on factors such as the ultimate location of the position and the selected candidate’s knowledge, skills, and abilities. Position may be eligible for additional compensation that may include an incentive program.
Job Description
** This is a remote position; however, candidates located within 25 miles of the Atlanta office will come in 3 days/wk. Candidates located in Atlanta preferred. **
The Sr. Director, F&I Dealer Operations leads the dealer-facing operations of Cox Automotive’s Dealertrack F&I business, with full ownership of the associated P&L, revenue budget, and overall business performance. This role also oversees the Express Aftermarket business, including revenue growth, provider network management, and strategic provider relationships.
As the voice of the dealer, this leader develops and executes strategies that drive market share growth, dealer satisfaction, operational excellence, and commercial success. The role partners closely with Product, Technology, Sales, Operations, and Finance teams to translate dealer needs and market trends into business priorities and measurable results.
The Sr. Director is responsible for optimizing the systems, processes, and support structures that enable efficient, compliant, and scalable F&I operations, including digital contracting, credit application processing, contract administration, and third-party service management. The position drives continuous improvement initiatives that enhance financial performance, streamline operations, improve dealer experience, and support the industry's transition from paper to digital workflows.
The role also establishes and enforces operational policies, monitors service and performance metrics, manages operational, financial, and compliance risks, and serves as an executive representative for the dealer business with internal stakeholders, dealers, lenders, and external partners. Success in this position requires strong business leadership, strategic thinking, operational expertise, and a commitment to delivering profitable growth and exceptional dealer outcomes.
POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES
Dealer Business Leadership & Growth:
Provide executive leadership and own the P&L for the Dealer Solutions F&I dealer business and Express Aftermarket, holding day-to-day accountability for delivering the revenue budget, operational effectiveness, and alignment with Dealer Solutions strategic objectives.
Develop and execute the business strategy to grow F&I market share and dealer penetration, including dealer acquisition, retention, and cross-sell strategies across Cox Automotive solutions.
Develop and lead cross-collaboration strategies with CAI matrix partners, fostering a high-performance culture and creating opportunities to build the dealer customer base and drive product revenue.
Contribute to the development and enforcement of operational policies and procedures, ensuring alignment with corporate standards and applicable regulatory requirements governing dealer/lender financing operations.
Ensure efforts are in place to streamline and optimize business service processes – including administrative, transactional, contract administration, and vendor management support – leading to greater effectiveness and efficiency across F&I operations.
Monitor dealer business performance metrics – including revenue, market share, dealer retention, and dealer satisfaction – ensuring high-quality service delivery and ongoing adaptation in response to evolving F&I business and operational needs.
Represent the F&I dealer business from an executive perspective, engaging with internal clients, boundary partners, dealers, lenders, and third-party service providers to ensure mutual and shared understanding of departmental objectives, practices, and delivery expectations.
Identify potential risks associated with business service delivery – operational, financial, compliance, and fraud-related – developing and overseeing implementation of mitigation strategies.
Develop and manage revenue and operating budgets for the F&I dealer business, ensuring operational and resource efficiency.
Work closely with Finance and F&I business management, ensuring effective dealer business contribution from a bottom-line perspective.
Voice of the Customer:
Serve as the voice of the dealer for the F&I business, establishing structured feedback loops (e.g., dealer advisory input, surveys, CSAT/NPS, support and attrition insights) and translating dealer needs into prioritized requirements for Product & Technology.
Maintain a close understanding of evolving dealer trends, F&I market dynamics, and competitor offerings; advise executive leadership on market opportunities, threats, and Cox performance versus the competition.
Manage key dealer relationships, resolve service delivery challenges, ensure consistent delivery of the desired dealer experience, and connect dealers with other areas of Cox Automotive to address cross-product issues.
Business Enablement & Continuous Improvement:
Develop business cases for strategic F&I initiatives, including ROI projections, resource requirements, and prioritization of activities according to strategic value.
Translate F&I dealer business strategy into actionable, well-sequenced improvement plans, providing project management oversight and accountability for key initiatives.
Set clear metrics for improvement initiatives and implement a process to measure progress, ensure accountability, and recognize success.
Lead change management for dealer-impacting initiatives, identifying requirements, enabling change readiness, and removing barriers to adoption.
Recommend changes to capability requirements and capital investments, leveraging deep market expertise to support business case development.
Express Aftermarket & Provider Network:
Own the Express Aftermarket business and its revenue, setting strategy and annual plans to grow dealer adoption and transaction volume of aftermarket products through Express.
Partner with Sales, Marketing, and Product & Technology to drive dealer awareness, adoption, and usage of Express, using dealer and provider feedback to improve the experience.
Recruit and onboard new aftermarket providers and products to the Express network, prioritizing additions that increase value and usage for dealers.
Negotiate and manage commercial terms, pricing, renewals, and agreements with aftermarket providers, ensuring contract compliance and mitigating risk.
Build and maintain executive-level relationships with aftermarket providers, leading business reviews, resolving issues, and monitoring provider performance and satisfaction.
Lead and develop the Express Aftermarket provider relationship manager responsible for day-to-day provider account management.
F&I Operations & Business Services:
Oversee administrative and transactional support underlying F&I product delivery, including credit application processing, digital contracting operations, contract/document preparation, approval, and distribution, and dealer and lender billing and invoicing.
Manage contract administration and negotiation support for F&I-related vendor, lender, and service-provider agreements, ensuring compliance with contract specifications and regulatory requirements.
Support operational execution of F&I transformation initiatives, including migration from paper-based to digital contracting and simplification/rationalization of F&I product and billing structures.
Ensure business service systems are in place to support fraud prevention, compliance monitoring, and risk-mitigation workflows relevant to F&I operations.
Leadership:
Direct the efforts of subordinate managers and professional staff within the F&I Dealer Operations organization, fostering a high-performance culture.
Build and maintain executive-level relationships with key dealers and dealer groups, aftermarket providers, internal customers, vendors, lenders, and stakeholders, addressing concerns and ensuring delivery of high-quality, value-adding services.
Lead efforts to leverage technology to streamline processes, address concerns, and further enhance service delivery.
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS & SKILLS
Job Family Functional Skills (Mastery / Advanced level):
Accuracy and Attention to Detail – Mastery: processes information with high accuracy; develops tools and checklists to ensure error-free output; accurately gauges impact and cost of errors and applies lessons learned.
Business Acumen – Mastery: applies deep knowledge of economic, financial, market, and industry trends to shape F&I dealer business strategy, grow market share, and limit risk.
Budgeting – Mastery: creates accurate, realistic budgets; monitors and adjusts budgets to reflect business change; identifies, explains, and reports on planned versus actual discrepancies.
Contracts Management and Administration – Mastery: manages and administers contractual agreements; ensures vendor/lender data and files are created, stored, and managed as required; reviews contracts for compliance.
Customer Focus – Mastery: understands dealer, lender, and internal customer needs; sets priorities and takes action to prevent service issues; tracks experience, captures voice-of-the-dealer feedback, and drives improvement.
Internal Controls – Mastery: creates, implements, and enhances processes for effective internal control; ensures compliance with company standards and legal/regulatory obligations.
Job Family Foundational Skills (Mastery / Advanced level):
Builds Positive Relationships – Mastery
Communicates with Consideration – Mastery
Focuses on Execution – Mastery
Guides Team Success – Mastery
Makes SMART Decisions – Advanced/Mastery
Domain / Additional Skills:
Deep knowledge of dealer F&I operations, automotive industry trends, dealer behaviors, and enabling technology; working knowledge of lender operations, including digital contracting, credit application processing, and fraud-prevention workflows preferred.
Demonstrated track record of growing revenue and market share in a B2B software or services business.
Knowledge of the F&I aftermarket (e.g., vehicle service contracts, GAP, and ancillary products) and the provider/administrator landscape preferred.
Advanced people-leadership skills; demonstrated experience directing the efforts of subordinate managers and professional staff.
Strong vendor and contract negotiation, renewal, and risk-mitigation experience.
Excellent verbal, written, and executive-level presentation skills; ability to advise and influence senior leadership.
High level of proficiency in MS Office applications, including Word, PowerPoint, and Excel.
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS
Bachelor’s degree in a related discipline and 12 years’ experience of progressive experience in business operations, general management, or dealer-facing operations leadership, ideally within automotive software, dealer finance, or F&I environments. The right candidate could also have a different combination, such as a master's degree and 10 years’ experience; a Ph.D. and 7 years or 16 years’ experience of progressive experience in business operations, general management, or dealer-facing operations leadership, ideally within automotive software, dealer finance, or F&I environments.
7+ years experience in which the individual assigned and prioritized others’ work, reviewed and approved final deliverables, and provided *performance input, including feedback and coaching. Below are examples of qualifying leadership experience: Formal lead or team lead role
Oversight of contract, contingent workers, interns, suppliers, or vendors
Matrix or dotted-line leadership; Formal mentorship of junior team
Demonstrated P&L ownership, including developing and managing revenue and operating budgets, vendor, lender, and provider contracts, and business processes at an enterprise or major business-unit level.
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
MBA preferred.
Experience supporting regulatory, compliance, or risk-mitigation requirements within a financial services or dealer/lender-facing operating environment preferred.
Experience in businesses based on technology, software, or digital solutions for the automotive or related industry preferred.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION REGARDING THE POSITION
Reporting Relationships : This role reports to the VP, Business Development and F&I.
Travel Requirements : Up to 10–15%, as needed to support dealer, aftermarket provider, vendor, and lender engagements.
Key Client & Internal Partner Interfaces : F&I Dealers and Dealer Groups, Sales, Sales Business Office and Marketing, Product & Technology, Client Operations, Finance, Legal, and Supply Chain, Lender Partners, Aftermarket Providers, third-party vendors and service providers.

Job Description:
What It Means to Be a Consultant at Crowe
Consulting is a dynamic business focused on solving problems for our clients and serving our core markets through innovative solutions. As technology and AI continue to reshape the consulting landscape, we are looking for individuals who are curious, adaptable, and eager to learn. The AML & EDD Financial Crime Review Analyst is responsible for performing transaction activity reviews, investigations and customer due diligence reviews on customers that have been alerted for potentially suspicious activity, potential sanctions list matches or that have been identified as posing elevated risk for money laundering and terrorist financing. They will be responsible for ensuring that reviews and investigations are maintained at a level commensurate with regulatory expectations. This role will assist in Suspicious Activity Reporting (SAR), and/or enhanced due diligence (EDD) reviews on customers identified as posing a higher inherent risk and/or sanctions screening.

Reviewing and investigating alerts, performing investigations, or enhanced due diligence reviews for potentially suspicious activity, making risk-based SAR recommendations and preparing SARs.

Reviewing and investigating potential matches with sanctions lists.
Maintaining a solid working knowledge (functional and operational) of the rules and regulations, including but not limited to, BSA, USA PATRIOT Act, OFAC and Sanctions Screening.
Assist in the delivery of financial crime consulting services to Financial Services companies, including Banks, Money Service Businesses (MSB’s), Third Party Payment Providers, and FinTechs.
Handle other duties as assigned.

Strong writing, analytical, and communication skills and the ability to multi-task and complete projects on time.
Strong research skills and sound knowledge in the use of the Microsoft Office Suite and experience with on-line research systems including the Internet.
Knowledge of client and transactional monitoring processes.
Detail oriented with the ability to multitask and quickly adapt to changing assignments.
Ability to work autonomously and with teams in different locations.
Highly effective communication with all levels of the organization.
Ability to anticipate, draw conclusions, and adapt to changing needs and demands.
Excellent verbal, written and interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with all levels of staff and management.
Strong analytical skills, problem solving, strategic thinking and reasoning abilities.
A high degree of integrity, professionalism, and capacity to excel in a cohesive team environment.

Associate’s degree and/or Bachelor’s Degree.
Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialists (CAMS), or other relevant professional certification.
Experience performing AML and financial crime investigations, customer due diligence reviews and/or sanctions screening reviews.
Experience working in AML software solutions including transaction monitoring systems, customer risk rating systems, and/or case management tools like Actimize, Verafin, Fiserv, FCRM, Jack Henry Yellow Hammer, Patriot Officer.
General banking compliance knowledge.
Experience working in a professional services or project-based environment.
Expertise in common financial crime technology platforms like CLEAR, LexisNexis, World Check etc.

As technology and AI continue to reshape the consulting landscape, we are looking for individuals who are curious, adaptable, and eager to learn. At Crowe, consultants are expected to build both technical and transferable skills, think critically, and use technology to solve real business problems. In this role, you will continuously learn, collaborate across teams, and explore how tools, including emerging AI capabilities, can improve efficiency, insights, and client outcomes.
As you grow, you’ll also begin to take ownership of client relationships, contribute to account strategy, and support the delivery of high-impact work. Developing a sense of account leadership, including understanding client needs, ensuring delivery excellence, and building trusted partnerships, is part of what sets successful consultants apart.
Success in this role comes from a growth mindset, strong communication skills, advanced critical thinking, and the ability to navigate new challenges with confidence.
As Salesforce Consultant with Crowe, you will play a key role on our project team by bridging the gap between business problems and technical solutions for our clients. You will engage directly with customers to understand their needs, design custom solutions, deliver & implement innovative real-world solutions. You will be expected to provide consultative advice regarding industry best practices and create a solution that always best meets our client’s needs.

Pre-sales scoping, supporting a Solution Architect/Sr. Consultant, as needed
Documenting business requirements, functional requirements & technical requirements in a pre-sales environment to generate a solution and Scope of Work, as needed
Work closely with key stakeholders (internal & client facing) to capture business needs, define requirements for the scoped work and clearly outline the affected business processes
Assist in fully solutioning scopes of work that meet business needs in a clear and cohesive manner, with oversight from SA/SC
Work at discretion of SA/SC for project implementation & architectural design by both solutioning and delivering on workstreams as identified & assigned

Entity Relationship Diagrams and Data dictionary
Current state and future state process flows
Wireframes and mockups
Use declarative functionality to build solutions & complete all assigned project actions using Salesforce and Crowe best practices
Assist in project delivery once work is completed by completing QA of all work, compiling change sets for deployment & assist in building all documentation for the client
As you continue to grow in your role and work further towards becoming a more independent consultant, you will lead smaller projects on your own from end to end with oversight from SA/SC

Our ideal candidate will possess the following skills
Competency & experience with Salesforce core products
Drive and desire to learn and grow both technical and functional skill sets and expand knowledge of the Salesforce platform
2+ years’ minimum experience on the Salesforce platform
Experience managing & delivering multiple projects at the same time
Detail-oriented, enthusiastic, self-starter with ability to work both independently and in a team environment
Strong, dynamic communication skills - both written & verbal - with ability to work cross-functionally and speak to members at any level of an organization (both client & prospect)
Ability to log time on a daily basis for client and project reporting needs
Positive minded, solutions-oriented approach and outlook is critical
Ability to work - and thrive - in a fast-paced, high-growth, innovative environment
This position requires a minimum of 20% travel
Bachelor’s degree

Willingness to obtain Certification in Salesforce Admin and one of the Consulting Cloud certifications.

The Manager, Tax Transaction Advisory Project Manager leads the operational execution, coordination and performance management of complex tax transaction engagements and private equity client relationships. This role serves as a central point of accountability for engagement governance, cross-functional service delivery, resource and workflow planning, financial reporting, and continuous improvement. Working closely with tax, transaction services, audit, advisory and relationship leadership, the Manager translates strategic priorities into disciplined execution, provides actionable insights on engagement economics and capacity, and helps deliver a consistent client experience across the deal lifecycle and recurring compliance services.
Client Account & Engagement Leadership
Lead cross-service-line coordination and recurring account reviews, aligning transaction, compliance, audit and advisory teams on commitments, deliverables and client priorities.

Oversee engagement-letter workflows, scope documentation, conflict-check coordination, signature completion and consistent engagement setup practices.
Transaction Lifecycle & Delivery Governance
Direct project management infrastructure for M&A tax engagements, including workplans, deal trackers, document request lists, SharePoint workspaces, standardized deliverables and retention controls.
Coordinate closing and post-close activities, including invoices, payment follow-up, closing documentation, remediation items, voluntary disclosure agreements and transition into recurring compliance.
Maintain deal-roll visibility, facilitate handoffs across teams and surface follow-on service opportunities to relationship and service-line leaders.

Standardize project trackers, time-entry codes, workflow tools and reporting routines to improve transparency, consistency and accountability.
Lead planning and monitoring of milestones, resource assignments, work-in-progress, planned versus actual hours and delivery bottlenecks; escalate capacity or execution risks promptly.
Coordinate critical tax data flows and K-1 delivery dependencies among portfolio-company, fund and individual tax teams.
Financial Management & Performance Analytics
Support engagement budgets, proposal development, rate-card consistency and forecasts of resource demand and financial performance.
Oversee engagement billing coordination, accounts-receivable visibility, aging escalations and fee-related independence tracking in partnership with appropriate leaders.
Leadership & Stakeholder Partnership
Drive process improvements and adoption of standard practices across teams without compromising client service, quality or compliance requirements.
Act as a trusted operational partner to TTA leaders, providing concise management reporting, decision support and proactive risk identification.
Coordinate stakeholders across tax, transaction services, finance, legal, compliance and other service lines to resolve issues and keep engagements on track.
Qualifications
Experience managing complex projects, client-service operations or professional-services engagements, preferably in tax, transaction advisory, accounting or consulting.
Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional initiatives, manage competing deadlines, influence stakeholders and communicate with senior leaders.
Strong financial and analytical acumen, including budgets, billing, utilization, realization, margins and operational performance reporting.
Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint and workflow/reporting tools; familiarity with Workday or comparable professional-services systems is beneficial.
Excellent judgment, organization, attention to detail and commitment to confidentiality and high-quality client service.
Measures of Success
Predictable delivery against engagement milestones and timely resolution of risks and escalations.
Improved visibility into capacity, chargeability, realization, margins and receivables.
Consistent adoption of standardized engagement processes, documentation and account reporting.
Effective handoffs from transaction close to recurring services and stronger cross-service-line collaboration.

title: Assistant Site Manager
description:
About the Team
DashMart is a local-fulfillment center owned and operated by DoorDash, offering customers household essentials and other items to their doorsteps with speed, reliability, and quality.
About the Role
In this role, you’ll work within a 5-15k sq ft distribution center, will assist in leading the local warehouse operating team, and in some locations, includes preparing food in a light-prep kitchen, and help the Site Manager ensure we maintain high quality for our customers.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Lead: You’ll demonstrate compassion and commitment to inclusivity as you lead a team of hourly Operations Associates and Shift Leads. You’ll hire, coach and develop high-performing team members, while building a safety-first culture where employees are excited to drive success, personally and for the team. You’ll serve as a leading change agent for your site, helping your team to navigate new initiatives and growth projects. You’ll tackle onsite escalations, including coordination with cross-functional partners.
Operate: With your thumb on the pulse of all outcomes for your team, you will be directly responsible for driving results in one or more specific focus areas or a specific shift for your site. To achieve your performance targets, you’ll drive success through effective scheduling and by executing inventory management processes and deploying best practices from across the network. You’ll engage cross-functional partners as needed for support.
Strategize: Within the focus area(s) assigned by your Site Manager, you’ll analyze data and make strategic recommendations and execute actions regarding resource allocation, workflow, warehouse organization and when to engage cross-functional partners. You may also lead some process improvement projects.
Delight: We are customer-obsessed. You’ll coach and empower your team to provide a highly quality customer experience with every order. Quality metrics such as order accuracy and fulfillment speed will be key measurements of success for your team. You’ll also work cross-functionally with central teams from our inventory to training teams to ensure your team has the tools and resources they’ll need to deliver.
We’re excited about you because…
You’re a proven leader. You have managed high-performance teams of 5+ employees with successful performance and employee development outcomes.
You relish ownership. You’re excited to have ownership in a new and rapidly growing business. No problem is too big or too small for you, and you’re ready to show up however needed for your team.
You solve problems from first principles.   You’re excited to solve problems in innovative ways, and you resist “this is how it’s always been done” thinking.
You’re unafraid of ambiguity.   Rapid change and learning is exciting to you, and you thrive in ambiguous, startup environments.
You’re analytical . You let data win arguments. You are a data-first problem solver and you have experience using Excel or Google Sheets to analyze data, including using basic formulas and creating pivot tables.
You have 3+ years’ experience : In Operations, Warehouse Logistics, Customer Service, Retail Management, Fulfillment, or related field
You have 1+ years of experience managing a team
You have flexibility in your schedule. As the leader of the site, you will need to ensure your team and the site is fully supported, which will include regularly scheduled late-night and weekend hours.
Compensation
Actual compensation within the pay range listed below will be decided based on factors including, but not limited to, skills, prior relevant experience, and specific work location. Base salary is localized according to employee work location.
DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits package to all regular employees, which includes a 401(k) plan with employer matching, 16 weeks of paid parental leave, wellness benefits, commuter benefits match, paid time off and paid sick leave in compliance with applicable laws (e.g. Colorado Healthy Families and Workplaces Act). DoorDash also offers medical, dental, and vision benefits, 11 paid holidays, disability and basic life insurance, family-forming assistance, and a mental health program, among others.
To learn more about our benefits, visit our careers page here .
See below for paid time off details:
For salaried roles: flexible paid time off/vacation, plus 80 hours of paid sick time per year.
For hourly roles: vacation accrued at about 1 hour for every 25.97 hours worked (e.g. about 6.7 hours/month if working 40 hours/week; about 3.4 hours/month if working 20 hours/week), and paid sick time accrued at 1 hour for every 30 hours worked (e.g. about 5.8 hours/month if working 40 hours/week; about 2.9 hours/month if working 20 hours/week).

At DoorDash, our mission to empower local economies shapes how our team members move quickly, learn, and reiterate in order to make impactful decisions that display empathy for our range of users—from Dashers to merchant partners to consumers. We are a technology and logistics company that started by enabling door-to-door delivery, and we are looking for team members who can help us go from a company that is known as the place you order food to a company that people turn to for any and all goods.
DoorDash is growing rapidly and changing constantly, which gives our team members the opportunity to share their unique perspectives, solve new challenges, and own their careers. We're committed to supporting employees’ happiness, healthiness, and overall well-being by providing comprehensive benefits and perks including premium healthcare, wellness expense reimbursement, paid parental leave and more.
Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion
We’re committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That’s why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

Whether blatant or hidden, barriers to success have no place at DoorDash. We value a diverse workforce – people who identify as women, non-binary or gender non-conforming, LGBTQIA+, American Indian or Native Alaskan, Black or African American, Hispanic or Latinx, Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander, differently-abled, caretakers and parents, and veterans are strongly encouraged to apply. Thank you to the Level Playing Field Institute for this statement of non-discrimination.

DoorDash for Business is building the premier corporate dining and benefits platform—helping companies of all sizes feed their teams through industry-leading products and meal programs. Our mission is to become the go-to solution for executives, administrators, and employees who need seamless, high-quality food programs at work. As an Associate Manager on the DoorDash for Business Catering team, you will own the Dasher and delivery experience for catering—making sure large, high-stakes catering orders show up on time, get handed off and set up correctly, and reach the customer the way they expect.
You'll work at the intersection of operations, logistics, and analytics—getting deep into the details of how catering deliveries actually play out on the ground, forming hypotheses about what's breaking, and running small, fast tests to find what works before we scale it. You have 4–6 years of experience in strategy & operations, logistics, management consulting, or a high-growth marketplace environment.

About the Role
The Sort Capacity Manager owns network-wide capacity de-risking for the Sort organization. This role builds and maintains the constraint model that defines what “de-risked capacity” means across every 1P and 3P facility — dock door availability, floor/pallet-position space, max throughput, and optimal labor and automation.
About the Team
Own the network constraint model — Model site capacity against its underlying constraints: dock door availability (inbound/outbound truck cadence by hour, translated from Mx forecast), floor/pallet-position space (inbound-to-outbound hourly volume vs. staging capacity), max throughput (automation vs. manual sortation rate, package profile mix, cross-dock vs. sort), and optimal labor hours required to hit max output.
Govern spoke capacity data — Drive spoke capacity maintenance in the sort app, ensuring product reflects current facility configuration, and hold cross-functional partners accountable when it doesn't.
Own zip-to-facility strategy — Own zip code-to-facility mapping and re-optimization as volume and rates shift, balancing service-level and cost trade-offs.
Own device and consumable readiness — Forecast scanners, bins, and gaylords against site growth to avoid reactive procurement; own the readiness cadence end to end.
Scope hub-to-spoke routing opportunities — Build the business case for hub-sort-to-spoke direct routing and bring recommendations forward to Network Design and Real Estate.
Close forecasting product gaps — Identify where forecasting tools fail to capture capacity reality and drive the fix with Data/Product partners.
Own Mx launch — Own Mx launch end to end, including CET allocation by merchant priority, negotiating trade-offs across competing merchant demands.

3-6-12 month runway visibility ahead of any projected capacity constraint.

Experience — 7+ years in supply chain, network strategy, or operations, with direct experience owning capacity planning or site launch strategy at scale.

title: Senior Associate, Operational Intelligence, Labs
description:
About the Team
DoorDash Labs builds autonomous delivery robots and other autonomy solutions for DoorDash’s delivery platform. Operational Intelligence is a technical team within our Technical Operations organization, developing the internal applications, data integrations, and AI-powered workflows that help our robotics fleet operate reliably and efficiently. We work directly with fleet support, service, Engineering, and Product teams to turn operational challenges into practical technical solutions. Our work makes information more accessible, improves troubleshooting and decision-making, and reduces the manual effort required to support a growing fleet. Being embedded within Operations means we stay close to the people using our tools and see the impact of what we build.
About the Role
As a Senior Associate, Operational Intelligence, you will build and maintain applications, integrations, and automation that improve how our teams operate. This is a hands-on individual contributor role within Technical Operations, with software development as a core responsibility. We are looking for someone who brings strong systems experience: understanding how frontend and backend services fit together, how APIs connect them, and how software is built, deployed, and operated in production.You will own defined features and projects from understanding the operational problem through development, testing, rollout, and ongoing support. This role is suited to someone who enjoys writing code, investigating system behavior, and working directly with users to deliver solutions that remain useful and reliable after launch.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Design and build full-stack features, connecting frontend interfaces to backend services and data stores, with a clear understanding of how requests, authentication, and data move through the system.
Instrument services with logging, metrics, and alerting so failures are detected and diagnosed quickly.
Partner with DoorDash Engineering and platform teams to align Operational Intelligence systems with company infrastructure standards.
Work directly with operational users to identify recurring challenges, translate feedback into technical requirements, and deliver improvements from concept through rollout.
Develop integrations and data workflows using APIs, databases, and automated jobs to connect systems, improve information quality, and reduce manual handoffs.
Contribute to AI-powered troubleshooting and decision-support capabilities, evaluating their accuracy, usefulness, reliability, latency, and operating cost.
Use version control, code review, automated testing, and staging environments to validate changes before deploying them into operational workflows.
Investigate application and integration failures, identify root causes, implement fixes or mitigations, and communicate findings to the appropriate stakeholders.
Improve operational reporting by validating data relationships, metric definitions, and outputs used to inform decisions.
Create technical documentation, troubleshooting guides, and user resources so others can confidently use and maintain the solutions you build.
Measure the impact of your work through adoption, time saved, reduced manual effort, and improvements in workflow quality.
Play a lead role in transitioning the Operational Intelligence team’s systems to a production-grade architecture, from design decisions through migration.
Mentor Operational Intelligence Associates to assist in the growth and development of the Operational Intelligence team (code quality, testing best practices, and documentation standards, etc.)
We’re excited about you because…
You’re excited to apply your development skills within an Operations organization and work closely with the people who depend on the systems you build.
You have 3–5 years of hands-on experience developing and maintaining software that runs in production environments.

You have experience designing and consuming REST APIs.
You have experience deploying and operating containerized applications (Docker, Kubernetes).

You’re comfortable using the command line, and collaborating through Git, GitHub, and issue-tracking tools.
You approach problems with curiosity and a root-cause-first mindset, distinguishing immediate workarounds from durable improvements.
You communicate clearly with technical and nontechnical audiences, write useful documentation, and explain progress, tradeoffs, and results.

description:
About the Team
The DoorDash Air team is bringing drone delivery to reality. To make this happen, we’re building a strong electrical team to design high reliability, high power density converters, and fault-tolerant controls electronics. Come join us to build a new class of aircrafts and deploy at scale.
DoorDash Labs, established in 2018, serves as the innovation hub for DoorDash, focusing on developing automation and robotics solutions to enhance last-mile logistics. The team's mission is to create technologies that support and augment human networks, aiming to improve efficiency for Dashers, merchants, and consumers alike.  We’re ruthlessly focused on business impact.  We are a highly senior team composed of former pioneers from a variety of different robotics industries.  As of 2025, DoorDash has completed 10B lifetime deliveries.  We’re focused on how to do the next 10B even better.
About the Role
We're hiring a Senior UTM Engineer who will build core components of DoorDash Air's internal route planning and airspace deconfliction stack — the systems that decide where our aircraft can safely fly, coordinate that with other operators and airspace authorities, and keep our internal stakeholders and external systems talking to each other in terms they understand. This is a role for someone who has already lived through the full lifecycle of a distributed, interoperable, uptime-critical system in a field where getting it wrong has real consequences — aviation, finance, communications, healthcare, or similar — and wants to bring that judgment to a fast-moving aerial delivery network.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Design, build, and deploy interoperable services that must pass rigorous, often open-source, conformance and integration testing against external systems and partners.
Develop novel path planning and airspace deconfliction algorithms that find safe, efficient routes through real-world, dynamic environments.
Build tools that help our teams and systems evaluate and optimize airspace efficiency and utilization.
Design integrations that connect the deconfliction stack to existing DoorDash systems, translating mission and airspace status into terms internal stakeholders can act on.
Collaborate closely with systems engineering, commercial operations, and flight operations to ship features that hold up in real-world flight.
Represent DoorDash Air externally — engaging with peer companies, working groups, and standards bodies to improve interoperable deployments industry-wide and help shape the
We’re excited about you because…
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field.

You've built and shipped production services that had to interoperate with systems you didn't control, including passing external or open-source conformance/certification testing.
You have hands-on experience with path planning, routing, or deconfliction problems in real-world, dynamic environments — or the algorithmic depth to pick this up quickly (graph search, optimization, or motion planning fundamentals).
You're comfortable building evaluation and analysis tooling, not just the systems being evaluated — you like giving other teams visibility into system performance and efficiency.
You can design clean integrations across organizational boundaries and translate technical system state into language that commercial, operations, and non-engineering stakeholders understand.
You communicate well with non-technical stakeholders and are comfortable representing your work and your company outside of it — in standards working groups, industry forums, or direct collaboration with peers at other companies.
You have strong software engineering fundamentals and experience with the languages and paradigms common to safety- and uptime-critical distributed systems (e.g., C++, Python, Go, or similar, plus familiarity with real-time or fault-tolerant system design).
BS/MS/PhD in CS, EE, Aerospace, Robotics, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

Experience with airspace management, air traffic control, or UAS traffic management (UTM) concepts and systems.
Experience contributing to or engaging with technical standards bodies or open-source interoperability efforts.
Familiarity with certification-aware development processes (e.g., DO-178, ARP4761) common to safety-critical aerospace software.
