title: Customer Success Manager
description:
Who we are:
Formic is on a mission to reshape American manufacturing by making automation accessible to every factory. As labor constraints rise, costs increase, and global competition intensifies, automation is no longer optional for manufacturers that want to stay competitive.
We deliver automation through a Robotics-as-a-Service model that combines industrial robotics, proprietary software, and full-service support into a single, integrated solution. By removing the traditional barriers of cost, complexity, and risk, we enable manufacturers to deploy automation quickly and realize measurable gains in throughput, safety, and operational efficiency without large upfront capital investment.
Backed by leading investors including Lux Capital, Initialized Capital, Blackhorn Ventures, and Mitsubishi HC Capital North America, Formic is scaling rapidly and building the foundation for a new era of high-performance, Made in America production.
About the Customer Success team:
Customer Success is dedicated to enabling our customers to get the most out of the automation we deploy, facilitating a superb experience through all facets of our relationship. We are manufacturing and automation experts–consulting with customers to drive adoption and optimal usage of our robotic automation solutions, and identifying opportunities to continue their automation journey.
As Customer Success Manager , you will serve as the primary point of contact and advisory partner for our customers: visiting and consulting with those customers in the field, and driving solutions across various groups within Formic for optimal delivery of technical, operational, training and administrative support for our industrial robot systems.
You will play a key role in driving mutually beneficial customer relationships post-deployment by monitoring customer health and engagement, mitigating potential relationship and experience risks, and identifying growth opportunities in existing accounts. You will build and maintain strong customer relationships; develop a deep understanding of their business goals, challenges, and needs; and will leverage that feedback to provide customized insights and value-added products and services. This position is highly strategic and impactful in Formic’s mission to be a valued partner and leader driving the adoption of automation across the manufacturing industry.
Internally, you will act as the voice of the customer within Formic, delivering feedback and recommendations internally to drive product and process improvements to yield better outcomes and experience. You will be instrumental in equipping Formic’s various teams to consistently deliver high performance automation solutions with superb customer experience.
As Customer Success Manager, you will:
Serve as the primary consultative partner and point of contact for the group of customers you are responsible for: building strong relationships; facilitating technical, operational, training, and administrative support; and identifying opportunities for expansion.
Oversee a regular cadence of communication and site visits (including regular travel throughout your region) to assess satisfaction with deployed robotic automation systems, address relationship issues, facilitate and offer training, solicit feedback, and identify opportunities for growth and improvement.
Monitor & manage health and engagement by using diagnostic tools and strategic communication, identifying and mitigating potential relationship and experience risks.
Collaborate with Formic’s Sales, Deployment, and Service teams to guide customers - particularly first time automation buyers - through their automation journey.
Identify opportunities for growth of products and services within existing accounts, including deployment of additional like-for-like solutions, or upstream or downstream standard solutions.
Leverage understanding of customers’ businesses to provide feedback for new product offerings and service enhancements for Formic to better serve their needs.
What makes you a great fit:
3-5+ years of experience in a manufacturing operations role (e.g. Plant or Production Manager/Supervisor/Process Engineering Leader) in a manufacturing or production operations environment.
Familiarity with robotic automation systems in a manufacturing or production environment (e.g. robotic automation of palletizing, de-palletizing, case packing, machine tending, welding, injection molding).
Outstanding communication and stakeholder management skills–able to build trusting relationships with diverse stakeholders and audiences and collaborate cross-functionally
Strong judgment and calm execution during escalations, shifting priorities, and time-sensitive customer needs
Ability to identify expansion opportunities through strong relationships, customer insight, and operational outcomes
Proficiency with CRM and customer relationship management tools such as Salesforce, ticketing systems, or project tracking platforms
Strong operational discipline, follow-through, and ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously
Experience working with industrial, manufacturing, hardware, robotics, or operationally complex customers preferred
Experience working successfully with a portfolio of industrial automation users leading to adoption, expansion and renewals preferred–ideally of technical platforms and solutions
Consultative sales experience is a plus
Ability to travel ~30% of the time to customer sites across their region, living in close proximity to a major airport
Holding a current, valid driver’s license and access to a vehicle

At Formic, we believe people do their best work when they feel supported both professionally and personally. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits and perks package for full-time, U.S.-based team members, including:
Equity in Formic: Participate in our stock option program and share in the success of a fast-growing start-up backed by leading global investors
Competitive & Uncapped Commission Structure: Designed to reward performance and impact in commission-eligible roles

Formic’s pay and equity packages are thoughtfully benchmarked against peer companies at a similar growth stage. Equity represents a meaningful part of our mutual investment: when Formic succeeds, so do you.

Build Formic's brand within manufacturing while ensuring our marketing investments support clear commercial objectives.

Own the creation of qualified pipeline across Marketing, lead generation, SDR/outbound, ABM, events, paid, organic, partnerships, and emerging channels.
Establish clear pipeline goals and build repeatable systems to identify, engage, and qualify manufacturers that fit Formic's ideal customer profile, optimizing channel mix, conversion, and resources.
Lead and develop our Sales Development function, including targeting, prospecting strategy, messaging, sequencing, coaching, productivity, and performance.
Establish clear funnel definitions, ownership, lead routing, and follow-up processes to ensure every source of inbound and outbound interest is captured, acted upon, and effectively handed off to Sales.
Partner closely with Sales and RevOps on territory priorities, pipeline needs, lead quality, conversion, and feedback from the market.
Measure pipeline contribution, progression, conversion, and cost by source and channel, connecting marketing investments to closed-won revenue and informing where to invest, optimize, or stop.
Build Our GTM Innovation Capability
Lead our GTM Engineering capability, using AI, automation, data, enrichment, personalization, and emerging technologies to improve how we identify, reach, engage, and qualify potential customers.
Own the effectiveness and evolution of our marketing technology ecosystem, including CRM integrations, outbound platforms, lead routing, data quality, attribution, and reporting, in partnership with Sales and RevOps.
Build and optimize scalable systems for account identification, segmentation, prospecting, personalization, campaign execution, and lead management.
Evaluate existing tools and workflows, identifying opportunities to simplify, automate, integrate, consolidate, or eliminate work rather than defaulting to additional tools or headcount.
Drive disciplined experimentation across channels, technologies, data sources, and approaches, establishing clear hypotheses, measurable outcomes, and decisions about what to scale, change, or stop.
Ensure our GTM infrastructure is reliable, documented, and maintainable, with clear ownership, appropriate data governance, and minimal dependency on any single person or external partner.
Own the Funnel and the Numbers
Establish clear visibility into the entire funnel, from target account through qualified opportunity, pipeline progression, and revenue.
Define and own a focused set of metrics that measure pipeline creation, conversion, velocity, cost, channel effectiveness, and commercial impact.
Partner with Sales and RevOps to ensure reliable data, consistent reporting, and a shared understanding of performance.
Establish a disciplined operating cadence that translates performance insights into decisions about strategy, priorities, budget, and resources, holding the organization accountable for outcomes rather than activity.
Create Focus and Accountability
Translate broad company objectives into clear priorities, ownership, expectations, and measurable outcomes that connect the team's work to business goals.
Make disciplined decisions about priorities and resources, challenging assumptions, stopping initiatives that aren't delivering results, and adapting as we learn.
Stay close enough to the work to identify problems early, remove obstacles, and hold people accountable without becoming a bottleneck to execution.
Foster a culture of transparency, constructive challenge, and open communication about performance, priorities, tradeoffs, and lessons learned.
Establish accountability for external agencies, contractors, and technology partners, including deliverables, performance, costs, documentation, and continuity, while building sustainable processes that preserve institutional knowledge and support organizational change.
Build and Lead the Team
Lead and align a multidisciplinary organization spanning Marketing, content and creative, lead generation, Sales Development, and GTM Engineering around shared commercial goals.
Build a high-performing team by establishing clear expectations, delegating meaningful ownership, coaching and developing talent, and addressing performance gaps directly.
Assess existing capabilities, recognize and develop the strengths of the people already here, and determine what additional skills and resources we'll need as we grow.
Hire thoughtfully and build organizational capabilities that create leverage, rather than adding unnecessary layers or headcount.
Foster a culture of creativity, curiosity, accountability, experimentation, and continuous improvement, where people feel empowered to challenge assumptions and solve problems.
What Makes You a Great Fit:
Experience building and leading Marketing, Growth, Demand Generation, or similarly broad functions in high-growth B2B companies, with measurable commercial results.
A track record of building, improving, and scaling marketing and pipeline-generation systems, not simply inheriting and managing established operations.
Deep understanding of B2B demand generation, funnel economics, segmentation, conversion, attribution, and how Marketing, SDR, and Sales work together to create and convert pipeline.
Experience developing differentiated positioning and messaging for complex products, markets, and buying decisions.
Strong technical fluency and demonstrated experience evaluating, integrating, and optimizing marketing technology, data, automation, and AI-enabled GTM systems, with the ability to diagnose problems and make informed architectural decisions.
An AI-native mindset, with demonstrated ability to apply emerging technologies, experiment rigorously, evaluate results, and turn successful approaches into scalable capabilities.
Strong people leadership, including building and developing teams, delegating meaningful ownership, addressing performance gaps, and leading effectively through growth and organizational change.
An operating style that combines creativity, analytical rigor, intellectual flexibility, and accountability, with the judgment to challenge assumptions, make difficult tradeoffs, and change course when evidence warrants it.
The ability to operate strategically and tactically, creating clarity from ambiguity, communicating effectively across functions, and staying close enough to execution to understand and solve problems.

Evaluate existing tools and workflows, identifying opportunities to simplify, automate, integrate, consolidate, or eliminate work rather than defaulting to additional tools or headcount.

title: Accounting Manager
description:
Job Description:
The Accounting Manager leads the US accounting organization and drives accurate, timely and well-controlled financial processes in compliance with ITW policies and US GAAP. The role owns the US accounting processes end to end (Invoice-to-pay, bill-to-cash and record-to-report), leads and develops the accounting team, and supports the Controller with forecasting, reporting and analysis. The Accounting Manager understands and champions ITW business model for accounting and reporting.
Scope and Team
Accounting for the US manufacturing operations, organized by process rather than by product portfolio.
Leads the US accounting team, currently including Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable and Staff Accountants.
Core Responsibilities
Process ownership and improvement
Own the design, documentation and performance of US accounting processes end to end, with clear handoffs, defined owners and measurable KPIs.
Lead continuous process improvement (toolbox), standardization and automation opportunities across the accounting function.
Partner with the Controller and IT on ERP and database integration, and on GL and financial statement reporting in Power BI.
Close and reporting
Own the monthly close calendar and coordinate with plants and functional teams to ensure timely, accurate financial statements in accordance with US GAAP.
Ensure timely entry of monthly and quarterly financials and the Tax Kit into the ITW corporate reporting software; review the work prepared by the team.
Perform and review monthly account reconciliations, including bank, intercompany, cost function and other reconciliations.
Perform detailed analysis of accounting information, monitor completeness and accuracy, identify potential problems, implement corrective actions and follow up until resolved.
Manufacturing accounting
Ensure accurate accounting for inventory, standard cost and variances (purchase price, labor, overhead), reserves and capitalization, working with plant finance and operations.
Internal controls and audit
Ensure documentation, monitoring and remediation of internal controls in accordance with ITW policies, including ICQ and the Top 13 Controls and segregation of duties.
Develop and maintain financial reporting processes that meet or exceed internal and external audit requirements; assist the Controller in internal and external audits.
Oversee the Procurement Card program (policy, card issuance and cancellation, credit limits, periodic reviews and training); day-to-day administration is performed by the AP team.
Planning and analysis
Support the Controller in the preparation of Quarterly Reviews, Long-Range Plan, Annual Plan, Critical Forecast, and business modeling and analysis.
People and business partnership
Lead, coach and develop the accounting staff, including goal setting and performance reviews.
Build team resilience through cross-training, back-up coverage and documented procedures, reducing dependence on any single person.
Act as business partner to leadership team members and plant management on finance-related topics.
Other duties as assigned.
Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or Finance required; CPA strongly preferred; MBA preferred.
7+ years of accounting experience in a manufacturing environment, including cost accounting, inventory and month-end close.
Demonstrated experience (at least 3 years) managing a direct staff of accounting professionals, including coaching, developing and leading a team through change.
Strong knowledge of finance, accounting, budgeting and cost control principles, including US GAAP and internal control frameworks.
Ability to analyze financial data and prepare financial reports, statements and projections.
Excellent knowledge of ERP and BI systems (Power BI preferred) and Microsoft Office, especially Excel.
Outstanding written and verbal communication, presentation and interpersonal skills, with the ability to relate to people at all levels.
Ability to multi-task, work under pressure and meet deadlines.
Demonstrated accountability for results and understanding of the financial impact of decisions.

$115,000-$123,000

title: CNC Programmer - 1st Shift
description:
Job Description:
The Mechanical Components Division is seeking a skilled and motivated CNC Programmer to join our Machining Team. The CNC Programming Team provides centralized, offline programming support for our machining operations and serves as a key technical connection between Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, and our customers.
This position plays an important role in developing and optimizing machining processes, supporting new product introduction and insourcing activities, improving existing manufacturing processes, and advancing machining technology throughout the department. The successful candidate will have strong machining knowledge, technical problem-solving skills, and the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, team-oriented manufacturing environment.
Key Responsibilities
CNC Programming and Process Development
Create, develop, and maintain Computer Numerical Control (CNC) programs.
Utilize CAD/CAM software to develop efficient, accurate, and repeatable machining processes.
Review and verify new and revised CNC programs for accuracy prior to release to the production floor.
Determine machining sequences, tooling requirements, work-holding strategies, cutting parameters, and other process requirements.
Optimize existing CNC programs to improve cycle time, tool life, quality, process capability, and overall manufacturing efficiency.
Troubleshoot complex machining and programming issues and support production with technical problem solving.
Support setup development, prove-outs, first-piece production, and process validation for new and revised components.
Engineering and New Product Support
Read and interpret engineering drawings, specifications, tolerances, and other technical documentation.
Conduct drawing reviews to identify errors, missing information, tolerance concerns, and opportunities to improve design for manufacturability.
Utilize SOLIDWORKS to review, interpret, and work with 3D part models and engineering design data in support of CNC programming and manufacturing process development.
Collaborate with Design Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Quality, and Operations on new product development and insourcing activities.
Serve as a technical resource and point of contact for customer engineering questions related to machining processes and manufacturability.
Assist with estimating machining cycle times, tooling requirements, process assumptions, and other technical information needed to support quotations.
Support Engineering Change Orders (ECOs), product revisions, and manufacturing process changes.
Manufacturing Technology and Continuous Improvement
Research, evaluate, recommend, and implement new machining technologies, cutting tools, work-holding solutions, programming methods, and manufacturing processes.
Identify and implement opportunities to improve productivity, quality, machine utilization, tooling performance, and manufacturing cost.
Partner with Engineering and Operations teams to drive operational efficiency and continuous improvement initiatives.
Support capital equipment projects, including equipment justification, process planning, installation, programming, runoff, and production implementation.
Assist with machine capability studies, process improvements, and corrective actions related to machining processes.
Documentation and Data Management
Create and maintain standardized operating procedures, setup documentation, tooling information, and other manufacturing process documentation.
Maintain CNC programs and associated documentation under appropriate revision control.
Maintain manufacturing data including drawing revisions, part weights, cycle times, and other process information within Microsoft Access and departmental systems.
Ensure programming and manufacturing documentation accurately reflects current production processes and adheres to current programming standards.
Production and Team Support
Prioritize programming workload to support daily production requirements, new product launches, engineering changes, and department priorities.
Work effectively both independently and as part of cross-functional teams.
Provide technical support and mentorship to machinists and production employees.
Assist with machining-related training and employee development initiatives.
Communicate effectively with operators, machinists, engineering, quality, leadership, and customers.
Maintain a clean and organized work area and support 5S initiatives.
Follow all company policies and procedures related to safety, quality, and operational excellence.
Perform other duties and special projects as assigned.
Qualifications
Required
High school diploma or equivalent.
Technical Certificate or Associate Degree in Machine Tool Technology or 5–7 years of relevant machining experience.
2–4 years of CNC G&M-code programming experience with proven ability to read and interpret G&M-code.
Strong machining and mechanical aptitude.
Demonstrated ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, GD&T, specifications, and manufacturing documentation.
Strong complex problem-solving and troubleshooting skills.
Ability to work independently and effectively within a team environment.
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
Effective written and verbal communication skills.
Computer proficiency, including Microsoft Office applications.
Preferred
Associate or bachelor’s degree in Manufacturing Engineering Technology, Industrial Engineering Technology, or a related field; or 10+ years of relevant manufacturing experience.
Experience with CAD/CAM programming software.
Experience using SOLIDWORKS for 3D model review, interpretation, and manufacturing support.
Experience with offline and centralized CNC programming.
Experience programming multiple types of CNC equipment, including turning and milling applications.
Experience with CNC process development, tooling selection, work-holding, and machining optimization.
Experience with Microsoft Access or similar manufacturing databases.
Technical Skills
Strong understanding of CNC machining principles, cutting tools, speeds and feeds, work-holding, and manufacturing processes.
Ability to develop and troubleshoot CNC programs using G-code and M-code.
Ability to interpret engineering drawings, dimensional tolerances, and GD&T requirements.
Ability to navigate and interpret 3D CAD models using SOLIDWORKS or similar CAD software.
Working knowledge of shop mathematics, including decimals, fractions, geometry, trigonometry, tolerancing, dimensional calculations, and unit conversions.
Ability to analyze machining processes and identify opportunities to improve cycle time, quality, tooling performance, and process capability.

The Field Service Engineer (FSE) services our Metal Detection, X-Ray and Checkweighing products at Loma’s customer sites throughout USA. The FSE does so in a manner consistent with Loma Systems policies and procedures while delivering exceptional customer service and promoting Loma Systems as the best in class organization.
a)   Essential Requirements :
High school diploma required. Associates degree from a technical school preferred.
Minimum 3 years of previous experience in a technical capacity or 4 years of military experience required.
Knowledge and experience working with electrical systems necessary.
Field travel experience preferred.
Knowledge of and experience in diagnosing, troubleshooting, and repairing electro-mechanical equipment and ability to identify root-cause.
Take pride in being organized with regards to completion of paperwork, expense reports, etc.
Ability to read, comprehend and interpret complex technical information involving mechanics and electronics. This includes interpretation of schematics and electrical diagrams.
Professional communication with an ability to resolve customer issues and defuse conflict.
Must be capable of a desire to learn a diverse set of products and continually improving product knowledge
Strong ability to use electronic test equipment such as multi-meters.
Ability to accept changes in a fast paced and changing environment; enjoy taking a hands-on approach in solving problems.
Work independently with little supervision while managing difficult and high-pressure customer situations.
Proficient with office software applications required.
Ability to work overtime
Physical & Environmental Requirements:
Must have a valid passport, a valid driver’s license and a good driving record.
Must be able to travel extensively (80% or more approximately) as required to service our customers.
Must be able to work within tight spaces and environments that may be noisy, odorous, dusty, cold and hot on a regular basis.
Must be able to lift and/or move up to 60 lbs. regularly.
Must be able to stand for long periods of time as well as walk, twist, bend, kneel, crawl, crouch, reach, climb and work in awkward positions on a regular basis.

Travel and deliver efficient field support to our customers.
Verify that machines are operating at peak efficiency by proper calibration and testing.

Promote sales of additional Loma product offerings such as service contracts, new equipment leads, spare parts kits, etc.

title: Flexographic Press Operator - 1st Shift
description:
Job Description:
We offer a safety-first culture, a clean work environment, and opportunity for pay and skill advancement through our operator level program.
Shift hours are Mo-Fr 6:00am to 2:30pm.
The Flexographic Press Operator is responsible to safely setup, operate, and maintain a multi-station printing press to produce high-quality print designs and lettering on flexible plastic film in accordance with specifications, procedures, and output requirements.
Essential Duties
Set up and operate multi-station flexographic (Flexo) press equipment, including changing rollers, adjusting doctor blades, installing cutting dies, and configuring temperature, speed, curing system, and tension via touchscreen and mechanical controls. Ensure accurate material registration and alignment.
Follow work instructions to prepare and load chemical mixes and inks. Conduct start-up checks and perform routine visual inspections of materials and equipment to ensure quality and performance standards are met.
Perform routine cleaning and maintenance of the press and rollers. Monitor operations and replenish chemical mixes and inks as needed to maintain continuous production.
Maintain accurate production, quality, and inventory documentation, including logbooks, work instructions, schedules, bar code labels, and work orders. Record quantities, footage, and specifications, and enter data into computer systems to generate labels for finished products.
Utilize precision measuring tools and equipment to support accurate machine setup and operation.
Prep material for conversion by monitoring and removing defects in editing department prior to setting up press.
Inspect print heads and materials for defects, taking corrective action as necessary to maintain quality standards.
Safely perform material handling tasks using lifts and hoists to move rolls, dies, and related materials.
Operate and maintain a variety of hand tools, including Allen wrenches, pipe wrenches, screwdrivers, box cutters, tape measures, and rulers.
Prepare UV and water-based ink and chemical mixtures in accordance with specifications.
Cross-train on additional equipment and batch mixing processes to support operational flexibility and team coverage.
Maintain a clean, neat, and organized work area, performing general housekeeping duties as required.
Strictly adhere to all safety, security, and company work policies and procedures.
Perform additional duties as assigned by the supervisor to support operational needs.
Qualifications
Our ideal candidate has a stable employment history, a positive and collaborative attitude, a desire to learn, and a demonstrated ability to work safely. Candidates selected for employment must pass a post-offer drug screen and background check.
The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
High school diploma or equivalent preferred.
3–5 years of experience in the setup, operation, and troubleshooting industrial machinery that continuously processes materials is preferred. Experience working with inks, printing processes, viscosity, hazardous materials (HAZMAT), and chemical weighing or mixing is strongly desired.
Material handling experience, including operating forklifts and scissor lifts.
Ability to follow both written and verbal instructions, including the ability to read and interpret technical drawings.
Basic experience using common hand tools and measuring devices.
Strong math and measurement skills, including proficiency with decimals and fractions, reading tape measures and scales, and understanding the metric system (grams, kilograms) with the ability to convert to standard units. Ability to read and apply formulas accurately.
Ability to work safely and independently with minimal supervision in a manufacturing environment.
ITW Covid Security (Cranbury, NJ) is a member of the ITW Specialty Films division of Illinois Tool Works (NYSE: ITW), a Fortune 300 global diversified industrial manufacturer.  ITW Specialty Films manufactures and markets specialized coated films for the Secure ID, Medical Specialty Bag, and Financial Card markets.   We offer a safe, clean work environment with a stable company and a dynamic, collaborative, and growth-oriented team.

Our employees enjoy a full benefit package which includes competitively priced medical plan options with FSA and HSA plans, dental, prescription drug, vision, 401(k) with a company match, life insurance, wellness programs, employee discounts, 12 paid holidays per year, vacation and sick time starting in year of hire, and a corporate matching gift program for charitable donations!

description:

Assembler: Assemble welding equipment through tasks such as engine preparation, base and front panel assembly, wiring, testing, and shipping. Rotate between tasks and help train others as needed.

title: Human Resources Coordinator
description:
Job Description:
Brooks Instrument ( www.brooksinstrument.com ), an industry leader in flow and pressure instrumentation for critical applications, is seeking candidates for a Human Resources Coordinator position that will be based at the company headquarters in Hatfield, Pennsylvania (suburban Philadelphia). The company has manufacturing locations in Pennsylvania, Hungary, Malaysia and Korea, and also maintains sales and service offices throughout the world. Our high-tech products are used in laboratory and process applications in end markets such as: oil & gas, petrochemical, medical devices, waste water, life sciences, and analytical instruments.
Brooks is a division of ITW (Illinois Tool Works), a fortune 200 company. ITW is one of the world’s leading diversified manufacturers of specialized industrial equipment, consumables, and related service businesses. The company has operations in 56 countries and employs over 50,000 employees. These talented employees, many of whom have specialized engineering or scientific expertise, contribute to ITW’s global leadership in innovation. The company is proud of its broad portfolio of nearly 10,000 active patents, and is focused on fully leveraging its highly differentiated business model to deliver solid growth with consistent best-in-class margins and return on capital.
Basic Function
The Human Resources Coordinator supports the day-to-day operations of the Human Resources
department, with a primary focus on hourly recruiting and onboarding. This position helps create a
positive experience for candidates, new hires, and employees by coordinating interviews, preparing for
new employee arrivals, maintaining accurate employee information, and responding to employee
questions.
The ideal candidate is organized, approachable, detail-oriented, and eager to learn. This is an excellent
opportunity for a recent graduate or an individual interested in beginning or growing a career in Human
Resources.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
Recruiting and Hiring
Support recruiting activities for hourly positions, from job posting through offer and onboarding.
Review applications and assist with identifying candidates who meet position requirements.
Conduct initial phone screens or coordinate candidate screenings as needed.
Schedule interviews and communicate interview details to candidates and hiring managers.
Coordinate pre-employment activities, which may include background checks, drug screens, and other required processes.
Maintain accurate candidate information and recruiting records.
Provide timely communication to candidates and help ensure a positive candidate experience.
Assist with job fairs, recruiting events, and other outreach activities.
Onboarding
Coordinate onboarding activities for new employees to support a welcoming and organized first-day experience.
Prepare and distribute new hire paperwork and monitor completion of required documents.
Communicate start dates, schedules, and other onboarding details to new hires and internal partners.
Coordinate with hiring managers and other departments to help ensure workspaces, equipment, and other resources are ready for new employees.
Assist with new hire orientation and follow up on outstanding onboarding requirements.
Maintain accurate and complete new hire records.
Employee Support and HR Administration
Serve as a point of contact for employees with questions about benefits, company policies, and general HR processes.
Assist employees with accessing benefits information and direct more complex questions to the appropriate HR team member or benefits provider.
Enter and update employee information and transactions in Workday, ensuring accuracy and timely completion.
Maintain employee files and handle confidential information with discretion.
Assist with HR reports, employee communications, and other administrative tasks.
Support benefits enrollment activities and employee meetings as needed.
Participate in other HR projects and initiatives as assigned.
Education and Experience
Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field preferred; an associate degree will also be considered.
Previous experience in HR, recruiting, or administrative support preferred.
Experience supporting hourly recruiting or working in a manufacturing environment is a plus.
Experience with Workday or another HR information system preferred.
Required Skills
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
Clear written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to manage multiple tasks, follow through, and meet deadlines.
Professional, approachable manner when working with employees and candidates.
Sound judgment and discretion when handling confidential information.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office, including Outlook, Word, and Excel.
Ability to learn new systems and work both independently and collaboratively
Benefits
Our employees enjoy competitive, merit-based salary plus excellent benefits including:
Health and dental insurance
Company Paid Life Insurance
Short and Long Term Disability
401K plan with generous company match
Vacation, personal days and holidays
Continuing education reimbursement program
Flexible spending accounts

title: AI Research Intern
description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.

Primary Function of Position
You will join Future Forward, Intuitive's advanced concepts group, and report to an engineering lead on the team building AI for the next generation of robotic-assisted surgery. You will own an open-ended research and prototyping project in areas such as supervised autonomy and automation for robotic-assisted surgery, and AI that helps care teams deliver care more consistently and efficiently. The work draws on computer vision, generative AI, robotics, and agentic AI, and we will shape the exact project with you based on your background and the team's priorities. A successful internship ends with a working prototype, clear evidence of how well it works, and findings the team can keep building on.
Essential Job Duties
Own an open-ended research and prototyping project, scoped with your mentor.
Explore how computer vision, generative AI, and agentic AI can be applied to new problems in surgery and the operating room.
Build working prototypes and evaluate them against clear baselines.
Work closely with researchers, engineers, and clinical experts.
Share your results through documentation and a final presentation and contribute to publications or patent filings where results warrant it.
Required Skills and Experience
Research or applied experience in at least one of computer vision, generative AI, robotics or autonomy, or agentic AI (LLM agents and tool use).
Strong Python skills and hands-on experience with a deep learning framework such as PyTorch.
A track record of taking a loosely defined problem to a result, shown through publications, open-source work, or projects others have used.
Sound experimental practice: you can set up a fair comparison and tell a real improvement from noise.
Clear written and verbal communication with both technical and non-technical audiences.

University Enrollment: Must be currently enrolled in and returning to an accredited degree-seeking academic program after the internship.
Internship Work Period: Must be available to work full-time (approximately 40 hours per week) during a 10-12 week period starting May or June. Specific start dates are shared during the recruiting process.
Required Education and Training
Current enrollment in a Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, Mechanical Engineering, or related degree-seeking program at the Doctorate level.
Master's level students would also be considered based on two or more years of relevant industry or research experience.
Working Conditions
None
Preferred Skills and Experience
Publications at leading venues such as CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CoRL, RSS, ICRA, or IROS.
3D vision, scene understanding, or spatial reasoning.
Generative models (for example diffusion or vision-language models) or LLM agents applied to real-world tasks.
Robot learning, robotics simulation (for example NVIDIA Isaac Sim/Lab or MuJoCo), or ROS 2.
Industry experience building ML or AI systems that other people relied on.
Interest in or exposure to healthcare, surgical, or medical robotics.

title: Health Economics & Outcomes Research (HEOR) Intern
description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position
The HEOR Intern will join Intuitive’s Future Forward Medical Affairs team for a 10–12 week summer internship, reporting to the Staff Epidemiologist, Future Forward Medical Affairs. The intern will own a defined, scoped real-world evidence project, using administrative claims data and reimbursement coding (CPT/HCPCS, ICD-10-CM/PCS, MS-DRG) to characterize patient populations, procedure volumes, healthcare resource utilization, and costs for a technology in development. Working alongside senior epidemiology, data science, and market access colleagues, the intern will contribute analyses that inform value propositions and may help translate findings into inputs for budget impact or other economic models. The internship culminates in a final presentation to Future Forward leadership and cross-functional partners.
Essential Job Duties
Real-World Data Analysis: With guidance from senior team members, conduct a retrospective claims-based analysis to characterize patient populations, estimate procedure volumes, and describe utilization, outcomes, and costs relevant to a Future Forward pipeline technology.
Coding & Cohort Definition: Identify and validate CPT/HCPCS, ICD-10-CM/PCS, and MS-DRG code sets to define target populations, procedures, comorbidities, and outcomes; document code lists and assumptions so they can be reused by the team.
Study Planning & Programming: Contribute to a brief study protocol and statistical analysis plan; write, document, and quality-check analytic code, partnering with the team’s data scientist on shared data pipelines.
Evidence Review: Conduct a targeted literature review to inform study design, benchmark findings against published evidence, and surface evidence gaps for the technology under study.
Economic Modeling Support: Where relevant, translate claims-based estimates (e.g., procedure volumes, event rates, costs) into inputs for budget impact or other economic models, and support model development or validation.
Communication: Summarize findings in clear visualizations and slides; deliver a final presentation to Future Forward leadership; contribute to a draft abstract where findings warrant.
Required Skills and Experience
Hands-on experience with reimbursement coding systems (CPT/HCPCS, ICD-10-CM/PCS, and MS-DRG), gained through dissertation research, research-assistant work, or prior employment, including using codes to define cohorts, procedures, and outcomes.
Demonstrated experience analyzing at least one large administrative claims or hospital database (e.g., Medicare MedPAR/SAF, MarketScan, Optum Clinformatics, Premier, PearlDiver, Komodo Health, or similar), from data extraction and cleaning through analysis.
Proficiency in SAS and/or R and working knowledge of SQL
Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to translate technical analysis for non-specialist audiences.
Comfortable working on a defined deliverable under the guidance of senior team members, with the independence to drive it to completion within the internship period.
Intellectual curiosity and comfort with ambiguity; this team works on problems that are not yet fully defined.
University Hiring Program Eligibility Requirements:
University Enrollment: Must be currently enrolled in and returning to an accredited degree-seeking academic program after the internship.
Internship Work Period: Must be available to work full-time (approximately 40 hours per week) during a 10-12 week period starting May or June. Specific start dates are shared during the recruiting process.
Required Education and Training
Current enrollment in a Health Economics, Health Outcomes/Services Research, Health Policy, Pharmaceutical Outcomes Research, Epidemiology, Biostatistics, or related degree-seeking program at the Doctorate (PhD) level.
Working Conditions
None
Preferred Skills and Experience
Experience developing or adapting budget impact models or other health economic models (e.g., cost-effectiveness, cost-consequence) in Excel, consistent with ISPOR good-practice guidelines.
Familiarity with Medicare payment methodologies (IPPS/MS-DRG, OPPS/APC, MPFS/RVU) and how coding drives payment across sites of service.
Research experience in medical devices, surgery, or procedural care.
Peer-reviewed publications or congress abstracts (e.g., ISPOR, AcademyHealth).
Experience with data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI).

The intern will identify, train, and test several RL algorithms using data collected from the Intuitive surgical robot systems. Position Overview
The Reimbursement Operations & Field Market Access lead is the execution engine of the U.S. HEMA organization. This role is the closest link to the sales and marketing organization and serves as the primary tactical interface with providers, payers, and field teams.
This is both a payer-facing and provider-facing role. On the payer side, this person develops value dossiers, manages payer advisory boards, and supports key account engagement. On the provider side, this person generates billing guides, fields customer reimbursement questions, develops provider education materials, and supports all field logistics related to coding implementation.
In Phase 1, this role carries both midstream and downstream responsibilities—from code acquisition and payment policy implementation through to field collateral generation and customer support. This person generates code and billing manuals, is responsible for all field logistics requiring implementation of new or existing codes, and directly fields customer questions regarding reimbursement.
This role carries shared responsibility for midstream/payment policy activities with the Upstream Strategist until a dedicated Midstream hire is made (~18 months). At that point, this role transitions to full downstream focus with outsourced or in-sourced field pull-through teams supporting product launches.
Core Responsibilities
Provider-Facing
Billing Guide Development: Create, maintain, and distribute comprehensive billing and coding guides for all products. Ensure guides are CPC-reviewed, compliance-approved, and updated with each code cycle.
Customer Reimbursement Support: Serve as the primary point of contact for management of customer reimbursement vendor(s).  Manage vendor, monitor performance, and retain required documentation.
Code Implementation Logistics: Manage all field logistics associated with the implementation of new or existing CPT, HCPCS, and ICD-10 codes. Coordinate with provider sites to ensure smooth adoption of coding changes and cost capture.
Sales & Marketing Support: Generate evidence-driven, compliant field collateral in direct support of the sales and marketing organization.
Payer-Facing
Value Dossier Development: Coordinate with Upstream and distribute value dossiers and payer-facing evidence packages that communicate the clinical and economic value of the product portfolio.
Key Account Management: Manage fractional headcount resources and coordinate payer engagement at key accounts.
Policy Monitoring & Implementation: Track payer coverage policies, MAC LCDs, and commercial payer guidelines. Translate upstream payment policy developments into actionable field tools and communications.
Field Personnel Management for Payer Campaigns: Manage and direct field personnel in support of payer-focused campaigns. Coordinate field reimbursement specialists, outsourced resources, and account-level teams to execute payer engagement strategies, coverage initiatives, and pull-through programs at targeted accounts.
Shared Midstream / Payment Policy
Code Acquisition Support: Support CPT/HCPCS code acquisition activities in partnership with the Upstream Strategist, including preparation of supporting materials for AMA and CMS submissions.
Payment Policy Implementation: Translate CMS OPPS/PFS payment policy changes into operational guidance for the field. Develop communications for code changes, payment updates, and coverage determinations.
Reimbursement Calculator & Tools: Develop and maintain compliance-accurate reimbursement estimation tools for use by the sales team and provider accounts.
Qualifications
Required
4 year degree is required.

Primary Function of the Position
Intuitive Surgical designs and manufactures highly complex mechanical systems for use in surgery. These systems include both capital equipment and “consumables” in the form of surgical instruments and accessories. The Senior Mechanical Engineer for Instrument and Accessory Advanced Product Development will be a member of a small team responsible for exploring and developing early product concepts and technologies that will help feed the da Vinci product pipeline. The successful candidate will lead early assessment, design, development, and testing of novel concepts for instrument and accessory related products.
The candidate will help to identify and evaluate new technologies in light of customer and company needs, establish design requirements to meet customer needs, work with suppliers and other outside companies and consultants to realize viable technical solutions, and refine designs for transfer to the New Product Development organization for commercialization. He/she/they must excel in a high-energy team environment and be capable of creative problem solving when faced with the time pressures and incomplete information typical of early- stage product development. The successful candidate must have outstanding technical depth in relevant areas , and be as comfortable collaborating and leading across organizational boundaries as they are working independently.
Essential Job Duties
Work within cross-functional project teams to create, evaluate, and prove out new product architectures and refine them for hand off to new Product Development
Collaborate with subject matter experts to understand the clinical, usability, and other needs of users of da Vinci systems as they relate to surgical instruments and accessories.
Develop technical requirements for designs based on an understanding of customer needs, commercial objectives (e.g. cost of goods), regulatory requirements, and feasibility constraints .
Perform conceptual design, detailed design, analytical modeling, prototyping, data analysis, and troubleshooting of novel instruments and accessories for the da Vinci robotic surgical system .
Develop and perform early performance testing, with assistance from other functions as needed. Assist with evaluation of prototypes by supporting bench, ex-vivo, and in-vivo laboratory testing with clinical experts.
Develop and manage relationships with key partners .
Provide written protocols, reports, and presentations related to design activities on an ongoing basis .
Review mechanical engineering designs of other Intuitive engineers in both a formal and informal capacity .
Refine and document product designs as needed to support successful transfer into the new product development organization.

Assess technologies from outside entities for potential licensing and adaptation to the da Vinci product line
Identify, test, and report on new materials, manufacturing processes, and technologies that could benefit existing products or enable new product designs
Document, prepare and review patent submissions

Minimum five (5) years of experience taking products from concept to production (medical product experience preferred).
At least eight (8) years of experience with precision mechanical design.
Familiarity with all phases of the product development lifecycle including design, implementation, debug, verification, qualification, and transfer .
Understanding of mechatronics, robotics, and servo-controlled systems strongly preferred. Experience developing software control algorithms a plus.
Proven ability to apply the basic laws of physics to understand and achieve quick and reliable solutions to engineering problems .
Exceptional mechanical aptitude and visual thinking skills .
Strong analytical and problem- solving skills such as finite element analysis, statistics, and experimental designs .
Strong understanding of design for reliability and manufacturability.
Proven ability to work well in a team environment and drive individual projects. Experience managing partners and small projects.
Proficiency using CAD to design and document mechanical designs. SolidWorks preferred.
Excellent verbal communication and presentation skills. Ability to present the work completed on his or her projects effectively
Ability to interface with customers and potential business partners in a highly professional manner
Comfortable with hands-on development work: Comfort operating standard machine shop equipment for prototyping (mill, lathe, etc.).
Proficient with techniques for rapidly fabricating proof-of-concept and functional prototypes.
Comfortable with standard mechanical and electrical measurement and test equipment .
Required Education and Training
BS (Mechanical Engineering or related engineering field) required, MS or PhD preferred .
Working Conditions
None
Preferred Skills and Experience
Experience and skills in design of high volume (e.g. injection molded, MIM) components, and design for manufacturability strongly preferred

The Sr. Director is accountable for the global indirect spend portfolio and for building a best-in-class procurement function. Essential Job Duties
The Sr. Director, Head of Global Enterprise Procurement leads the global indirect procurement function, partners closely with Finance, Legal, IT, Operations and Commercial leaders, and is a trusted advisor to the executive team on spend, suppliers and third-party risk. The Sr. Director will:
Vision, Strategy and Leadership
Develop and communicate a clear multi-year vision and roadmap for a best-in-class function, including operating model, capabilities, technology and talent.
Lead, mentor and develop the team across procurement operations, sourcing, contracts, and travel and events, with clear performance measurement, career paths and succession plans.

Shape demand upstream through standardization, policy and user education, and track value beyond savings, including stakeholder satisfaction, innovation and risk resilience.
Supplier Relationship and Risk Management
Rationalize the supplier base and build long-term partnerships with strategic suppliers, supported by a supplier performance and business review program.
Partner with Legal, Information Security, Quality and Compliance to manage supplier risk (financial, cyber, concentration, geopolitical and disruption) and to ensure contracts address regulatory and legal requirements.
Procurement Operations, Technology and Compliance
Continuously improve the source-to-pay lifecycle, including intake, sourcing, contracting, purchasing and payables, to reduce cost to serve, ease the stakeholder experience, and increase spend under management.

15+ years of progressive procurement experience, including 10+ years in indirect procurement with global responsibility and 5+ years leading teams in a large, publicly traded or comparable environment.

Demonstrated ability to develop high-performing teams, with a passion for developing and caring for people and a leadership style grounded in integrity and humility.
High commercial and financial acumen, with the gravitas to influence at the executive level and partner with Finance, Legal, IT and business leaders.
Seasoned negotiator with experience in complex, multi-million-dollar, multi-year agreements across diverse categories.
Strong data analytics skills, with a point of view on how AI and automation can transform procurement.
Expertise in source-to-pay systems and orchestration tools (Coupa preferred) and knowledge of procurement compliance, including SOX.
Excellent communication skills, able to translate complex sourcing issues into clear terms for suppliers, peers and senior leaders.

Willingness to travel 15-20%, including to Atlanta, Mexico, Europe and Asia Pacific.

Bachelor's degree in supply chain, business, finance, engineering or equivalent.
MBA or professional procurement certification (for example CPSM or CIPS) preferred.

description:

If you're ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare, you'll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position
We seek a StaffSystems Analyst to join the Future Forward Research group at Intuitive Surgical. Our group explores new, promising technologies for future products and applications in the emerging computer- and robot-assisted medical interventions field.
A Systems Analyst is responsible for the detailed design and implementation of controllers and algorithms to assess novel instrument concepts and visualization schemes running on Intuitive’s latest surgical robots or new platforms. This responsibility includes integrating and evaluating fully functional prototypes then promoting translation of concepts into finished products.
This position provides analytic assistance to other engineering groups to help design systems, software architectures, and interfaces. It maintains awareness and interest in developing research and technologies related to secure telerobotic and safety-critical systems and actively applies this knowledge to system design.
Essential Job Duties
This position is responsible for system software, algorithm development aspects, associated tooling, and infrastructure to explore and build new surgical platforms.
Develop and validate distributed electro-mechanical systems and dynamic models through targeted experimentation.
Design and implement software algorithms, tools, and infrastructure for new products.
Integrate mechanical, hardware, and software components for new product development.
Apply control system design methods to prototype and validate novel medical robotic systems.
Conduct comprehensive testing, safety analysis, and performance monitoring throughout the development lifecycle.
Lead early systems engineering development, requirement translation, and cross-functional discussions.
Develop sensor and control schemes to enhance robotic system performance and address user needs.
Apply best practices in software engineering and create thorough documentation.
Identify, document, and communicate intellectual property generated during development.
Required Skills and Experience
Strong theoretical and practical knowledge of robot manipulator kinematics, classical and modern control systems, teleoperation, and related algorithms.
A proven record of integrating and characterizing complete mechatronic systems.
Knowledge of electrical and mechanical design principles and CAD tools is a plus.
Experience designing and developing teleoperation algorithms and real-time embedded software systems.
Proficiency in Matlab and C/C++; experience with high-level languages such as Python and JavaScript.
Experience with computer vision processing pipelines and real-time implementation is a plus.
Ability to excel in a dynamic, focused team environment with a collaborative and positive approach.
Comprehensive understanding of teleoperation systems, software, and interfaces for building reliable, mission-critical solutions.
Skilled in profiling, debugging, and optimizing system software with a disciplined and persistent approach to problem solving.
Strong communication skills and commitment to teamwork.
Deep understanding of software engineering principles and methodologies.
Required Education and Training
A graduate degree in Electrical, Mechanical, Mechatronics, or Control Systems Engineering, or similar field relating to robotics or electro-mechanical systems.
A minimum of 7 years of experience in servo control systems development for robotics or electro-mechanical systems, with hands-on implementation.

title: Analytics and Intelligence Engineer
description:
Job Description:
Accelerator, a global Division of Mars Snacking, is on the front line of unlocking growth across high-potential categories and brands to fuel what’s next for Snacking. It’s home to both emerging and enduring brands, including KIND, TRÜ FRÜ, NATURE’S BAKERY, RXBAR, EGGO, POP-TARTS and RICE KRISPIE TREATS. Combining the scale of Mars with the agility of a start-up, our Division has the ambition to accelerate the future of snacking by delivering products consumers love today, discovering category-shaping innovations for tomorrow and developing entrepreneurial teams whose impact will last for generations.
We’re looking for passionate talent who dare to dream big, agile collaborators who talk straight and decide fast, and driven performers with a growth mindset. We’re proudly part of Mars, while also building something boldly different. If this inspires and energizes you, you’ve found the right place where you can do cool things with fun people for one of the biggest snacking companies in the world!
As an Analytics and Intelligence Engineer , you will be a key member of our collaborative Data and Analytics team, contributing directly to the design, development, and enhancement of Mars Accelerator division reporting, semantic modelling, and intelligence capabilities. You will partner alongside fellow engineers, data scientists, and business stakeholders across sales, marketing, supply chain, and finance to turn complex business requirements into dependable analytical data models and actionable dashboards.
In this role, you will help bridge business needs with robust data engineering practices, building high-quality data products, integrating predictive and automated intelligence into analytical workflows, and contributing to the continuous improvement of our modern analytics stack.
What You’ll Do
Partner with cross-functional business stakeholders and engineering peers to build consistent KPI dashboards, reliable data assets, and high-impact reporting tools.
Build, test, and maintain robust, scalable data models and semantic layers (using Star Schemas, dbt, and Databricks) that serve as a dependable single source of truth for the Mars Accelerator Division.
Collaborate with data scientists and analytics peers to incorporate predictive models, statistical forecasting algorithms, and anomaly detection into business-facing dashboards and semantic layers.
Actively follow modern software engineering best practices for data, including version control with Git, collaborative code reviews, automated testing (e.g., dbt tests, data quality validation), and continuous integration (CI/CD).

description:
Job Description:
Job: Production Leader
Shift: Nights
Location: Mars (Topeka, KS)
The Production Leader is a shift-based, front-line operations people Manager who efficiently improves Quality, Human Safety, and Product Cost Conversion while Engaging and Developing talent. The Production Leader is responsible for delivering operational targets and leading teams of, on average, 15 Shift associates.  The Production Leader drives safety, quality, continuous improvement, performance management, associate development, team engagement, and operating results for their assigned area through shift-based leadership of a line or area that exists within a larger Value Stream organization.
This leader coordinate the short-term activities of the area within established guidelines and standards to produce the highest quality, lowest cost product most safely and efficiently while also partnering with the other members of the 24-hour Area Managership Team to deliver area continuous improvement and Mars Supply Excellence (MSE) program implementation. The Production Leader is responsible for building an effective team on his/her shift and in his/her area of responsibility and for managing the training strategy for both the individual associates and the team. This leader will implement and enforce established policy and area and organizational strategies.
Key Responsibilities:
Conversion - Manage the efforts of multi-line, area, or technology operating teams on one shift to efficiently convert materials into quality products in a safe, secure, and sanitary manner within the product design specifications.
Change Agent - Implement changes in methods, equipment, systems, and organization, as needed, to ensure that the objectives of the line/area are met and give input and recommendations for such changes by using a continuous improvement mindset.
Mars Supply Excellence – Lead or participate in one or more MSE Pillars; Lead and support the implementation of Autonomous Maintenance (AM) and Autonomous Work Teams (AWTs) in area of responsibility; Lead key connection points and own reliability data collection accuracy.
Area Ownership – Collaborate with the rest of the Area Managership Team (Area Manager or Continuous Improvement Engineer, Continuous Improvement Specialist, Maintenance Coordinator) to create and execute the reliability strategy for the area of responsibility.
Coaching—Coach operators to build their functional and Managerial capabilities and drive accountability in safety, Quality and Food Safety, Autonomous Maintenance, and team engagement.
Line Operations - Coordinate materials, staffing, and resources to support line operation and changeovers.
Standards Implementation and Adherence – Ensure standards are implemented on shift and in areas of responsibility through effective communication, change management, consistent reinforcement, coaching, guidance, and accountability measures.
Associate Safety – Ensure safe working conditions, behaviors, and mindsets through the direct implementation of Mars Safety programs and driving a relentless focus among a team of operators.
Food Safety and Product Quality – Ensure the ongoing Shift of safe and defect-free products consistent with the principles of Mars.  HACCP proficiency is required; this manager owns ongoing training and championing of quality goals and improvements at the Area Shift level.
Associate Advocacy - Manage associate relations issues and guide and direct the hiring, training, retraining, development, and motivation of Operations associates following self-managed, team-working principles with a minimum degree of guidance from the Area Manager or Value Stream Manager.

Goal Setting and Measurement - With the general guidance of the Value Stream or Area Manager and/or the support of the Continuous Improvement Engineer, establish line and individual performance standards and goals, and measure, control, take corrective action, and report results as appropriate.
Troubleshooting – Utilize the technical resources on shift for the preventive maintenance, repair and troubleshooting of process/packaging equipment problems, to effectively use these resources to achieve desired performance levels.
Escalations - Proactively identify risks and opportunities and reactively lead on-shift incident resolution when operators require additional support. Prioritize, assign resources against escalated issues, and make decisions to resolve escalated issues.
Communications - Ensure that open communications are established and that opportunities to broaden the scope and responsibility of Operations teams/associates are undertaken.
Technology Advancement - Advise when opportunities exist for moving the line/area forward in technological change.
Operations Strategy - Participate in implementing improvement strategies to help the line/area perform more effectively in the near term.

description:

Job Purpose/Overview:
This role is responsible for performing all reception and unloading operations for raw materials coming into the manufacturing facility. This position will also handle master sanitation activities for the area and perform required inventory tasks.
Key Responsibilities:
Perform receiving and unloading of all raw materials (bulks, liquids, super sacks, bags).
Operate forklifts and other equipment to offload and store materials.
Manage and sign delivery documentation, noting any quality or quantity discrepancies.
Collaborate with the supply coordinator on inbound receiving priorities.
Accurately maintain the Warehouse Management System (WMS) and report any stock discrepancies.
Perform cyclical and period-end inventory counts of raw ingredients.
Conduct equipment verifications, record keeping, and first-level maintenance.
Uphold food safety standards and adhere to site Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs).
Execute sanitation duties as required by the Master Sanitation Schedule, following lock-out/tag-out procedures.
Promote a positive and high-quality team environment.
Qualifications:
Must be 18 years of age or older.
High school diploma, GED, or equivalent.
Willing and able to work varying shifts, schedules, and overtime.
Ability to work with minimal supervision and as part of a team.
Strong communication skills in English.
Preferred: 1 year of work experience in manufacturing or a related technical discipline.
Preferred: Competency in computer software, including MS Office, email, and inventory (WMS) systems.
Preferred: Knowledge of inventory control principles and ability to operate a forklift or scissor lift.
Physical/Environmental Requirements:
Ability to stand on a concrete floor for extended periods.
Must wear proper personal protective equipment (PPE).
Capable of bending, stooping, twisting, turning, reaching, and climbing stairs.
Ability to lift up to 55 lbs.
Must be able to adapt to temperature and environmental extremes (hot, cold, dust, dirt, chemicals).
Military Crosswalk: Transferable Skills
This position aligns well with the skills and experience gained in numerous military occupational specialties. Veterans bring valuable expertise in logistics, inventory management, and operations.
Relevant Military Experience:
The skills required for the Receiving Operator role are commonly found in the following (but not limited to) military logistics and supply fields:
Army: Automated Logistical Specialist (92A)
Unit Supply Specialist (92Y)
Cargo Specialist (88H)
Petroleum Supply Specialist (92F)
Air Force: Logistics Plans (2G0X1)
Materiel Management (2S0X1)
Air Transportation (2T2X1)
Navy: Logistics Specialist (LS)
Culinary Specialist (Submarine, Supply) (CSS)
Marine Corps: Logistics/Embarkation Specialist (0431)
Warehouse Clerk (3051)
Packaging Specialist (3052)
Coast Guard: Storekeeper (SK)
Transferable Skills:
Inventory Management: Experience with tracking, counting, and managing stock levels is directly applicable to maintaining the WMS and performing inventory cycles.
Logistics & Supply Chain: Military personnel are experts in receiving, storing, and issuing materials, which is the core function of this role.
Heavy Equipment Operation: Many military roles involve operating forklifts and other material handling equipment.
Attention to Detail: The military instills a high degree of precision, crucial for verifying shipments and maintaining accurate records.
Safety Compliance: Adherence to strict safety protocols, such as handling hazardous materials or following operational procedures, is a fundamental military skill.
Teamwork and Discipline: Working effectively within a team to achieve a common goal is a hallmark of military service.
We encourage veterans and transitioning service members with experience in these or related fields to apply.
Education & Professional Qualifications
Be 18 years of age or older
Have a high school diploma, GED, or equivalent education
Must be willing and able to work and accept varying shifts and schedules
Ability to understand and effectively communicate in the English language
Knowledge / Experience
3+ years of manufacturing experience operating a variety of machines
2 years of work experience within manufacturing, or a technical and/or trade discipline
Demonstrated competency in computer and pc software including MS Office and email
Knowledge of inventory control principles
Ability to operate a forklift and scissor lift

title: Regional Distributor Manager, U.S.
description:
Job Description:
Champion Petfoods is expanding! We are excited to announce we are looking for a Regional Distributor Manager, U.S. to join our rapidly growing company.
Champion Petfoods is an award-winning pet food maker with a reputation of trust spanning 35+ years. Founded in a small town in Alberta, Canada, Champion – with its ORIJEN® and ACANA® brands – is a key player in the global premium pet food industry across three major geographic regions.
We would love to hear from you if you are passionate about personal and professional growth and see yourself as a key player contributing to our continued success as an award-winning company.
Here's the Scoop – Summary
The Regional Distributor Manager, U.S. is accountable for delivering sales growth, market share expansion, distribution gains, and execution excellence through Champion's distributor partners within an assigned region.
Reporting to the Director, U.S. Sales, Neighborhood Pet, this role serves as the primary business lead for distributor performance and development.
The Regional Distributor Manager translates national sales strategy into regional execution plans, ensuring distributors and their sales organizations are aligned to Champion's priorities and growth objectives.
This position drives business results through distributor leadership, joint business planning, retailer engagement, sales capability development, and disciplined performance management.
Success in this role is achieved by building strong distributor partnerships, improving execution at retail, developing distributor sales teams, and delivering profitable growth throughout the region.
This is a fully remote position, which will ideally sit near Boulder (CO), Dallas (TX), Phoenix (AZ) or Southern California (CA). Expect 40-50% of travel within assigned geography.
Responsibilities:
Distributor Performance Ownership
Own sales, distribution, and execution result across assigned distributor partners and territories.
Hold distributors accountable to annual sales targets, distribution objectives, promotional programs, and strategic growth priorities.
Monitor distributor performance through established KPIs and implement corrective action plans when required.
Regularly evaluate distributor effectiveness, market coverage, resource allocation, and return on investment.
Distributor Strategy & Business Planning
Develop and execute Joint Business Plans with distributor partners aligned to national sales objectives and growth strategies.
Identify opportunities to increase market penetration, distribution points, retailer productivity, and share growth.
Lead annual planning, forecasting, and business review processes with assigned distributors.
Align distributor investments and resources to maximize commercial performance and customer impact.
Driving Execution Through Distributor Sales Teams
Influence, coach, and develop Distributor Sales Representatives (DSRs) to improve execution and sales effectiveness.
Conduct regular market visits to evaluate retail execution, merchandising standards, assortment compliance, and promotional effectiveness.
Deliver sales training, product education, and business development support to distributor sales organizations.
Ensure execution excellence against merchandising, pricing, promotional, and distribution objectives.
Retail Customer Development
Partner with key regional and independent retail customers to support growth, distribution expansion, and customer satisfaction.
Conduct customer business reviews and identify opportunities to strengthen Champion's market position.
Support distributor teams in developing retailer-specific growth strategies and action plans.
Build trusted relationships that position Champion as a strategic partner.
Forecasting, Analytics & Financial Management
Maintain accurate regional forecasts and provide timely updates on risks and opportunities.
Manage trade investments and promotional spending to maximize ROI and profitability.
Analyze sales performance, market trends, customer results, and distributor productivity to identify opportunities for growth.
Provide regular business updates and recommendations to the Director, U.S. Sales.
Market Leadership
Represent Champion Petfoods at industry events, trade shows, distributor meetings, and customer engagements.
Deliver insights regarding competitive activity, consumer trends, market dynamics, and emerging opportunities.
Partner cross-functionally with Marketing, Finance, Supply Chain, and Customer Service to ensure successful execution of business initiatives.
Key Accountabilities
The Regional Distributor Manager will be measured on:
Regional sales and profitability growth
Distributor performance against annual operating plan
Distribution gains and market penetration
Retail execution and merchandising compliance
Forecast accuracy
Trade investment ROI
Distributor sales force capability development
Regional customer growth and retention
Achievement of strategic business plan objectives
What are we looking for?
Bachelor's degree in Business, Sales, Marketing, or a related field.
5+ years of progressive sales experience within the pet industry, consumer packaged goods, or a related distribution-driven environment.
Demonstrated success managing distributor relationships and driving growth through indirect sales channels.
Proven ability to develop and execute business plans that deliver revenue growth, distribution gains, and improved customer performance.
Strong financial and commercial acumen, including forecasting, budgeting, business analysis, and ROI management.
Experience influencing and developing sales teams without direct reporting authority.
Excellent relationship-building, negotiation, and communication skills.
Ability to analyze market data and translate insights into actionable growth strategies.
Highly collaborative, self-motivated leader who thrives in a fast-paced and entrepreneurial environment.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and sales reporting tools.
Ability to travel approximately 40-50% within assigned geography.
Why You'll Succeed
You take ownership of results and hold yourself and partners accountable.
You know how to win through distributors and indirect sales channels.
You build strong partnerships while maintaining high performance expectations.
You balance relationship management with data-driven decision making.
You are passionate about developing people, growing customers, and delivering exceptional execution in the market.
Mars Leadership Competencies
Drives Results
Plans & Aligns
Balances Stakeholders
Financial Acumen
Interpersonal Savvy
Customer Focus
