Safety:   a strong commitment to ensure all people are provided with a safe, healthy and respectful environment.
Earnings:   Salary range from USD$115,000 to USD$158,000, 401k with Company, and donation matching.
Industry Competitive Benefits:   Medical, Dental, Vision and Employee Assistance Programs to meet your individual or family needs.
Continuing Education:   In House & Online Learning & Development, as well as an Education Assistance Program.
Quality:   a dedication to uphold the highest standards of authenticity, nutritional integrity, and food safety, to earn the trust of Pet Lovers everywhere.
Other Perks:   Free Bag of Premium Pet Food each month, Free Parking and more!
What are you waiting for? Join the pack!

We value diversity in all forms and know the power it can bring. Workplace equality allows for creative ideas to bloom, diverse points of views to be heard, and increases overall happiness. That sounds pretty good to us.

Strong mechanical troubleshooting and repair skills.

Combining the scale of Mars with the agility of a start-up, our Division has the ambition to accelerate the future of snacking by delivering products consumers love today, discovering category-shaping innovations for tomorrow and developing entrepreneurial teams whose impact will last for generations.

We’re proudly part of Mars, while also building something boldly different. Reporting to the Senior Marketing Director, KIND, the Sr. Brand Manager, Innovation owns what KIND launches next. This role leads a team of a Brand Manager and a Senior Associate Brand Manager, each owning a platform, and holds the earliest-stage bets personally until they earn an owner. The role works shoulder to shoulder with Consumer Research and R&D from the first consumer question to the final formulation, and hands the Core team launches that are ready to win.
What will be your key responsibilities?
Innovation Strategy & Portfolio Direction
Own the KIND innovation strategy: where the brand plays next across formats, occasions and adjacencies, grounded in a deep understanding of the consumer, their snacking needs and occasions, category dynamics and the brand platform.
Build and maintain the brand’s innovation insight foundation: who the KIND consumer is and could be, the jobs they hire snacks to do, the tensions and unmet needs in the category, and where KIND has the right to play.
Represent KIND innovation to Better For You leadership and global markets, building platforms that can travel and bringing market and consumer learning back into the pipeline.
Bring the Accelerator way of working into the brand: founder-style ownership, fast and cheap experiments, clear kill criteria, and the willingness to scale hard when something proves out.

Build and own the 18-month to 3-year pipeline, sequencing launches against capacity, investment and the commercial calendar so the brand always has news coming.
Own the stage-gate and Integrated Business Planning (IBP) steps and make the portfolio calls on what enters, accelerates, parks or stops. Decide early, decide with consumer evidence, defend the decision.
Build the business case for every launch, volume, margin, investment, incrementality and return, and partner with Finance to secure funding.
Own the early-stage bets personally from consumer insight through concept and validation until each passes a gate and earns an owner or stops.
Product Design & Development
Write propositions that start with the consumer: the problem, the person, the reason KIND wins, and the evidence that it will.
Lead product design across every component: formulation, format, pack structure and graphics, nutrition, taste and texture, naming and claims, so the product delivers the proposition in the hand.
Set the learning plan with Consumer Research for each platform, from concept screens through sensory and in-market validation, and stay close to the consumer throughout, in the research and in the field.
Partner with R&D as co-owners of the product on cost, capacity and ingredient trade-offs, and own the standard a KIND product must meet before it launches.
Launch Readiness & Cross-Functional Leadership
Hand each launch to the Core, Equity & GTM team at a defined point of go-to-market readiness, with proposition, product, business case and launch plan complete, and stay accountable for the first-year read.
Lead the innovation workstream across R&D, Supply, Finance, Insights, Category, Sales and Omni as one plan with shared milestones and KPIs.
Build and manage the external partnerships the pipeline depends on.
Talent & Capability
Lead and develop the Brand Manager and Senior Associate Brand Manager, giving each real platform ownership and cross-functional leadership.
Build innovation capability into the brand: faster concept testing, AI-enabled insight and ideation tools, and a repeatable path from idea to gate.
Bring the outside in: consumer and cultural trends, category, competitor and adjacent innovation, and what the brand can learn from how others are winning.

8+ years of progressive experience in Marketing, Brand Management or Innovation within CPG, with at least 4 years in an innovation role on a scaled consumer brand. Challenger brand, start-up or growth business experience is a strong asset.
Deep consumer understanding: has built innovation from a real consumer insight rather than a product idea, is fluent in qualitative and quantitative research, and can turn what consumers say and do into a sharp, ownable proposition.
Has taken a product from insight through concept, development, business case and launch, with clear accountability for the result in market.
Has run a multi-year pipeline and stage-gate process, including making and defending kill decisions.
Has led product design across formulation, format, pack, nutrition and sensory in deep partnership with R&D and Consumer Research.
Has managed external partners such as co-manufacturers, ingredient and technology suppliers or research institutions.
Builds business cases that hold up: sizes the opportunity, models volume, margin and investment, and can defend the number with senior stakeholders.
Has managed and developed people and led cross-functional teams without direct authority in a matrixed environment.
Entrepreneurial by instinct, with a bias for action, comfort with ambiguity and curiosity for how data and AI-enabled tools can change the speed and quality of innovation.

Represent Microsoft as an external technology voice at customer forums, government technology events, industry conferences, and executive briefings.

Plans, coordinates, and presents maintenance items for review and approval in their area of responsibility.

Performs inspections of equipment in a facility. Participates in testing and commissioning activities. Advises engineer partners or project management colleagues on project scope process or execution methodology. Presents for review and approval MSOW in their area of responsibility.
Acts as a subject matter expert, performing troubleshooting independently for multiple equipment, systems, subsystems, and component types. Documents issues found in troubleshooting process within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Ensures equipment and system settings are consistent with established parameters and designs. Determines when troubleshooting efforts are deemed adequate and communicates or escalates to suppliers, engineers, or more experienced colleagues as needed. Has a hands-on understanding of how equipment in all disciplines work and how to troubleshoot to subsystem level. Provides consultation to less experienced colleagues with troubleshooting systems and problems. Ensures troubleshooting completion paths are escalated appropriately and successfully by their team members. Oversees and advises their team members on troubleshooting systems and/or investigates root causes.

Understands critical system alarms for multiple discipline(s) of equipment, their meanings, and engages with appropriate escalation processes or procedures. Recognizes circumstances where execution would be considered safe to proceed. Performs various inspections and validations of equipment performance. Monitors the performance from central monitoring locations (i.e., Facility Operations Centers) of maintenance and operations of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, fire/life safety) and understands risks or impacts to other subsystems across the data center. Escalates per applicable policies and standards. Utilizes telemetry, control systems, and other platforms to monitor site status, analyze past and current events, as well as other processes, and can identify all alarms. Uses technical expertise, prior experience, and device analytics to recognize trends with equipment behavior and checks potential issues as they arise. Advises less experienced colleagues on issues found while monitoring applicable CE systems. Uses data trends to develop or produce predictive analyses of equipment performance.

title: Data Center Technician
description:
Overview
As a Microsoft  Data Center Technician  (DCT), you will develop an understanding of standard processes and procedures for preparing, installing, performing diagnostics, troubleshooting, replacing, and/or decommissioning equipment under the guidance of more experienced Data Center colleagues. Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 Data Centers in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide. With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our data center design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.
Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role’s job duties
Responsibilities
Datacenter Operations
Reviews Process Change Notifications (PCNs) and develops an understanding of the impact to work execution and awareness to changes within their area of work and/or the work of others. Asks questions when they do not have required information and may provide feedback on changes to processes to experienced technicians and/or direct-line management.
Completes assigned tickets efficiently and in alignment with relevant Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) per task type with guidance from experienced technicians. Seeks guidance from more experienced technicians on challenging or complex tickets.
Complies with Data Center business unit policies, procedures, and deadlines with guidance from experienced technicians and/or direct-line management. Escalates issues related to compliance or operational assurance activities to direct-line management.
Receives guidance and supervision to develop an understanding of standard processes and procedures for preparing, installing, performing diagnostics, troubleshooting, replacing, and/or decommissioning IT datacenter technology(ies) and equipment. Develops and acquires a fundamental understanding of the functions of, and interactions between cabling infrastructure, network, server, and storage equipment.
Datacenter Work Environment
Participates in daily safety briefings. Completes required Environmental & Health Safety (EHS) training, complies with safety procedures (e.g., equipment use, lifting, electrical hazards, ladder/rolling stair use), completes required Task Hazard Analysis (THAs), and uses appropriate equipment and Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) for assigned tasks. Adheres to and promotes a culture of safety, taking proactive action to alert others of safety concerns, near-misses, and/or incidents. Participates in the regular cadence of proactive safety observation reporting processes and systems.
Completes required security and data management training while complying with security and data management procedures/policies with guidance from other technicians. May escort third party vendors or IT support on-premises at data centers or network sites. Appropriately takes action and reports physical security access concerns and/or incidents to direct-line management or via established reporting methods.
Contributes to a positive and effective team environment by sharing information with other shifts or technician teams, contributing in regular team meetings, asking questions, and partnering with other shifts of technician teams to complete smooth transition and effective handover of ticketed work. Encourages providing and responding to feedback received on ways to work more effectively or enhance efficiency within their team and adopts best practices shared within-and-across shifts or technician teams

As indicated above, have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.
Managing Service
Maintains an awareness of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) through reporting dashboards, systems, for personal monthly performance discussions as needed.
Escalates and/or seeks guidance from experienced technicians or direct-line management regarding client interactions.
Develops an understanding of cross-functional Data Center processes to support partnerships with internal and external stakeholders.
Completes required training aligned to job focus areas and workloads (i.e., Break fix, Deployment, Simple Change, Decommission, IT Critical Environment) in a timely manner per direct-line management assignment(s). Observes more experienced technicians to gain hands-on experience and relevant on-the-job training (OJT). May complete additional or supplemental training to obtain or maintain relevant industry or technical certifications.
Physical Requirements
Applies to but is not limited to US-based Data Center roles: Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting 50lbs / 22.5kg. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg. with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.
Service Delivery
Develops an understanding of effective execution order strategy(ies) for assigned tasks with assistance from experienced technicians or direct-line management. Prepares, stages, sets up, and performs basic startups and shutdowns for hardware (e.g., racks, hard drives, switches) according to specific written instructions provided via checklists, guides, standard processes, emails, guidance from other technicians, and/or direction from management. May perform tasks in tandem with other technicians to comply with procedures and safety requirements.
Performs basic diagnostics and troubleshooting with guidance from experienced technicians and/or via standard procedures to identify the cause(s) of technical issues and replace faulty components in network, storage, or server equipment with zero-to-minimal customer and/or business disruption. Develops awareness of conditions, circumstances, and scenarios which may reflect significant customer or business impact within the Data Center environment.
Learns about post-execution verification of grounding, staging, labeling, and cabling to align with all safety protocols, deployment standards, and planned Network Design Templates (NDTs). Learns about errors in deployment standards or Network Design Templates (NDTs) and escalates to relevant technicians or specialists to coordinate corrections as needed.
Directly performs decommissions, simple changes (e.g., memory upgrades, OS rebuilds) and refreshes of infrastructure cabling, network, storage, and server equipment, following standard procedures whilst seeking clarification and guidance from more experienced technicians as needed. Processes data-bearing devices (DBDs) for destruction or confirms any-and-all such devices (e.g. hard-drives, solid-state drives, flash cards, etc.) contained within network, storage, or server equipment has been identified for eradication or destruction with guidance.
Follows procedures to immediately communicate, report, and escalate data center technical or safety related incidents to direct-line management. May participate in bridge calls to provide details on incident status and executes on-site follow-up actions as directed if necessary.
Working Conditions
Applies to but is not limited to US-based Data Center roles: Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.

Embodies our  culture  and  values .

High school diploma, GED, or equivalent and basic knowledge of computer hardware and components OR equivalent experience.
Other Requirements:
Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:

Specifically, this position supports United States federal, state, and/or local government agency customers and is subject to certain citizenship-based restrictions where required or permitted by applicable law. To meet this legal requirement, and as a condition of employment, the successful candidate’s citizenship will be verified with a valid passport.

High school diploma, GED, or equivalent and basic knowledge of computer hardware and components AND 1+ year(s) experience supporting IT equipment or related technology OR equivalent experience.

Define and run intake, approval, funding, authority, forecasting, and exception workflows in partnership with Corporate and Regional Finance.

Working closely with subsystem research and development leaders in areas such as control, packaging, and test and measurement, you will align roadmaps, manage risks, and deliver critical milestones. You will collaborate with physicists, quantum theorists, experimentalists, research and systems engineers, technical program managers, supply chain experts, cloud architects, and external partners to accelerate the scale-up of topological qubits and quantum systems. title: Senior Data Scientist for Copilot Evals
description:
Overview
CADET (Customer and Analytics Driven Evals Team) is building a customer-grounded quality system for Copilot. Our mission is to rapidly identify the customer scenarios that matter most, represent them faithfully in evaluation and learning assets, run quality gates continuously, and turn every important failure into reusable product and model improvements. We bring together DSAT and other product signals, deep customer engagements to create representative eval sets. Operating in a fast-paced environment, we connect customer grounded quality issues with quality teams to advance Copilot quality and product innovation.   We are looking for a Senior Data Scientist to build the measurement and decision system that determines where CADET invests and whether Copilot is improving for the customers and intents that matter most. You will combine DSAT, usage, customer engagement, product feedback, evaluation, and other quality signals to create a representation- and coverage-aware view of customer quality. You will define the taxonomies, metrics, prioritization models, analyses, and reporting mechanisms that turn a fragmented signal landscape into clear decisions. You will synthesize quality opportunities, investigate loss patterns, shape evaluation portfolios, and ensure recurring quality gates reflect real customer experiences rather than static benchmarks.   Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
Responsibilities
Build and operate a data-driven prioritization framework for CADET quality forums and partner teams that combines DSAT, customer impact, usage, severity, strategic importance, representation, and current evaluation coverage to guide quality investments.
Define and maintain intent, sub-intent, customer scenario, coverage, and loss-pattern taxonomies that can be used consistently across signal intake, triage, evaluation, and reporting.
Measure how well evaluation portfolios represent production traffic, customer segments, workflow complexity, locales, grounding paths, and material failure modes.
Identify underrepresented customers, intents, scenarios, and loss patterns, and translate those gaps into evaluation and data-collection priorities.
Design quality gates for top intents and top customers, including success thresholds, segmentation, run cadence, escalation criteria, and reporting.
Build recurring scorecards that connect offline evaluation movement with online measures such as DSAT, task completion, retries, abandonment, and escalation; detect meaningful quality changes; and alert accountable owners when action is required.
Analyze offline-online agreement, evaluation freshness, regression coverage, grader reliability, and quality movement over time.
Develop sampling, weighting, deduplication, clustering, and trend-detection approaches for noisy customer and product signals using resource- and performance-optimized data-analysis solutions that make effective use of CPU, GPU, and platform capacity.
Use causal and experimental methods where appropriate to distinguish correlation, attribution, and treatment impact, and translate the findings into concrete product, model, data, and evaluation investment decisions.
Partner to translate customer evidence into valid task distributions, datasets, metrics, and reward signals and to encode metrics, taxonomies, data-quality checks, and reporting into automated pipelines.
Leverage team signals from customer engagements to understand workflows, business impact, expected outcomes, and gaps hidden by aggregate metrics; produce clear recommendations for product, model, data, and evaluation investments; and communicate them to senior leaders.
Establish solid practices for data provenance, privacy, responsible use, reproducibility, and metric governance.
Qualifications
Required Qualifications:
Doctorate in Data Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Econometrics, Economics, Operations Research, Computer Science, or related field AND 1+ year(s) data-science experience (e.g., managing structured and unstructured data, applying statistical techniques and reporting results) OR Master's Degree in Data Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Econometrics, Economics, Operations Research, Computer Science, or related field AND 3+ years data-science experience (e.g., managing structured and unstructured data, applying statistical techniques and reporting results)

OR equivalent experience.
Preferred Qualifications:
Solid experience using data to shape product strategy and decisions in a complex, high-scale product or platform environment.
Expertise in SQL and at least one analytical programming language such as Python or R.
Solid foundation in statistical analysis, experimentation, sampling, segmentation, measurement, and data visualization.
Experience integrating noisy quantitative and qualitative signals into actionable prioritization or measurement frameworks.
Ability to define durable metrics and taxonomies, explain their limitations, and prevent misleading interpretation.
Demonstrated ability to communicate complex analysis clearly to technical, product, and executive audiences.
Experience with AI product quality, LLM or agent evaluation, DSAT or customer feedback analysis, experimentation, or model telemetry.
Experience designing representative datasets, coverage models, quality scorecards, or regression portfolios.
Experience with clustering, text analytics, embeddings, classification, anomaly detection, or other methods for mining unstructured feedback.
Experience connecting offline evaluation results with online product and customer outcomes.
Experience working directly with enterprise customers, researchers, product managers, and engineers.

Microsoft Frontier Company is a new operating business focused on helping customers achieve business transformation through AI by combining deep industry expertise, AI engineering capabilities, services delivery, continuous improvement, and outcome-driven execution.
Our team brings CI to Microsoft’s customer engagements, helping customers translate AI ambition into measurable business outcomes. We use structured problem solving and systems thinking to understand how work happens today and redesign end-to-end workflows across people, processes, and technology. title: Senior Partner Marketing Manager
location: United States, Multiple Locations, Multiple Locations
description:
Overview
The Senior Partner Marketing Manager leads the development and execution of integrated marketing and communications plans to drive strategic business initiatives, key change moments, and program activation across Microsoft's Global Partner and Channel ecosystem. You will work collaboratively with cross-company internal teams and the broader Microsoft channel partner community to craft and communicate a cohesive partner story that highlights the value across the partner lifecycle. You will be accountable for understanding program priorities, getting close to partner audiences to define content journeys that attract, enable, recognize, and retain partners, and developing integrated marketing and communications plans supported by clear measurement frameworks.
This role will collaborate closely with internal stakeholders to ensure alignment of messaging, timely execution of campaigns, and accurate reporting across a high-volume communications portfolio. You will think and act both strategically and tactically, using sound business judgment and a partner-first mindset to balance Microsoft's priorities with the needs of the partner ecosystem, particularly through periods of significant program change.
Responsibilities
Priorities:
Build and execute integrated marketing and communications plans, supporting content strategies and content journeys that promote the full value of partner motions. Ensure alignment to Microsoft business priorities, Global Channel Partner Sales (GCPS), Enterprise Partner Sales (EPS) and SME&C priorities across the partner journey, including build and GTM motions, enablement, change management activities.
Develop top-level narratives and messaging guides aligned to key partner moments to drive awareness, adoption, and recognition. Maintain the partner messaging and positioning framework and ensure consistency in storytelling across content channels and field engagements.
Create a comprehensive content plan with a core bill of materials (BOM) — anchored by the monthly partner emails and supporting nurture campaigns — that reflects partner and customer insights and provides clarity on how partners discover, engage with, and benefit from Microsoft partner opportunities, including clear paths to the web experience and Partner Center.
Define success metrics, measurement frameworks, and KPIs to report on impact and engagement — including email open and click-through performance against benchmarks, revenue retention and renewals (ARR and seat growth), lead activation and conversion, and tactic efficiency — to internal stakeholders across SME&C, GCPS, Marketing and EPS.
Drive operational excellence across the communications intake, planning, review, and launch process — partnering with agency teams to reduce churn, simplify complex processes, consolidate communications across pods, and accelerate time to market while improving the stakeholder and partner experience.
Ensure content and communications are delivered in accordance with Microsoft's privacy, security, and brand guidelines.
Manage agencies, vendors, and budgets to deliver content and campaigns aligned to defined business priorities, with a focus on fiscal accountability and compliance with Microsoft policies.
Support PR and communications as needed to ensure that partner programs are accurately and strategically represented across internal and external channels.
Be a partner advocate. Relentlessly champion Microsoft partners by ensuring their needs, experiences, and feedback shape content development and marketing strategies. Consider how partners discover, engage with, and apply content to grow their business and deliver customer success.
Contribute to the continual development of the team's marketing excellence by sharing top practices and insights, and by fostering an inclusive team culture where all employees can thrive and contribute to Microsoft's partner success strategy.
Qualifications
Required/minimum qualifications
Bachelor's Degree in Business, Marketing, Business Development, Business Management, Communications, or related field AND 5+ years sales, marketing, or business development experience OR equivalent experience.
Additional or preferred qualifications
Master's Degree in Business Administration, or related field AND 4+ years sales, marketing, technology-based, or business development experience OR Bachelor's Degree in Business, Marketing, Business Development, Business Management, Communications, or related field AND 6+ years sales, marketing, or business development experience OR equivalent experience.
8+ years of relevant experience in partner marketing, sales, or business development, ideally including channel or partner motions.
Proven ability to manage high-volume, multi-audience communications programs and collaborate across teams.
Experience developing campaign and segmentation strategies, assessing risk, leading change-management communications, and aligning execution with business priorities.
1+ years of experience in Cloud and AI workloads, incl. security
Strategic planning: Synthesizing research and insights to inform channel partner strategy and market positioning.
Partner-centered Learning: Evaluating internal/external data and engaging with partners to generate actionable insights.
Execution leadership: Driving execution of a high-volume marketing and communications portfolio, aligning with channel motions, and leveraging incentive programs.
Data-driven optimization: Using campaign performance data and partner segmentation to target at-risk and high-opportunity partners, mitigate revenue loss, and continuously improve outcomes.
Change management communications: Landing complex program, compliance, and new-commerce changes with clarity to drive timely partner action.
Cross-functional collaboration: Working across product, sales, field, operations, and agency teams to deliver integrated partner experiences.

title: Senior Product Manager
description:
Overview
Enterprises are rapidly increasing their use of AI agents, but many still lack a clear way to understand what agents they have, what those agents are doing, and whether administrative policies are being enforced.
Microsoft Agent 365 is building the core platform to address these needs across agents, tools, MCP servers, and models. The capabilities we build support experiences across the Microsoft 365 admin center, Cowork, security, FinOps, and partner integrations.
We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to own a major area of Agent 365 Core. This person should be comfortable working across platform, product, and engineering boundaries and should have recent, hands-on experience building with AI.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
Responsibilities
A major Agent 365 priority
Own the strategy, roadmap, and outcomes for one of our core areas: AI Registry, AI Observability, AI Governance and Enforcement, OnboardingYou will also connect your area to the broader platform so admins get one coherent experience rather than a collection of separate features.
Platform contracts
Define and drive the entity models, signal contracts, governance APIs, or onboarding patterns that Microsoft and partner teams depend on. Make clear decisions about what belongs in the platform, what belongs in individual products, and how the pieces work together.
Cross-company alignment
Drive decisions with teams across Entra, the Microsoft 365 admin center, Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry, Purview, Defender, and our partner ecosystem. Many of these teams will not report to you, so success will depend on clarity, technical depth, and follow-through.
Measures and accountability
Define the measures that show whether the platform is working, including coverage, freshness, verified enforcement, and time from a partner decision to the first usable signal. Publish the scorecard and use it to drive decisions.
Customer and partner discovery
Work directly with enterprise IT and security leaders, as well as partner developers. Translate their scenarios into reusable platform capabilities rather than one-off solutions.
Hands-on AI work
Use AI as part of your day-to-day work. Build prototypes, run evaluations, analyze data, and regularly demonstrate what you are learning. Help the PM team use agents effectively for research, specifications, and analysis while maintaining a high bar for accuracy and quality.
Show us your AI work
Along with your resume, include a link to a short example of your work. This can be a document of up to two pages, a repository, a deck, or a five-minute video.
Please cover the following:
1. Something you built with AI
Share a prototype, agent, tool, automation, or analysis you built. What problem did it solve? What did you use? What decision or outcome did it influence? Include links or examples where possible.
2. A process you improved with AI
Describe a process you changed for yourself or your team. What did the process look like before and after, and what measurably improved?
3. A time AI output failed
Describe a time when AI-generated output was incorrect, generic, or unsupported and progressed further than it should have. How was it caught? What was the impact? What guardrails did you put in place afterward, such as evaluations, grounding, review checkpoints, or team norms?
4. Your operating rules
If you were leading a PM team working alongside AI agents, what three rules would you establish to get the benefits without compromising quality?

Experience shipping platform or infrastructure capabilities that other teams build on, including APIs, data models, developer platforms, telemetry and observability, identity, or policy systems.
Recent hands-on experience building with LLMs, agents, MCP, and evaluations, ideally within the last 12 to 18 months.
A track record of aligning multiple engineering and product organizations without direct authority.
Experience working with enterprise IT and security leaders, partner developers, or ISVs.
Strong data skills. You can write and validate queries in KQL, SQL, or a similar language, including queries developed with AI assistance.
Strong written communication. Our specifications are read by engineers, partners, executives, and AI agents.

title: BIM Designer & Coordinator
description:
About the Team

Industrial Compute is building the world's most advanced AI infrastructure. Working alongside our capital partners, engineering teams, and construction organizations, we design and deliver large-scale, mission-critical compute campuses that power the next generation of AI. Our Design organization brings together engineering, construction, and digital design to ensure facilities are coordinated, constructible, and optimized from the earliest planning phases through deployment.

About the Role

We are seeking a BIM Designer & Coordinator to support the planning and design of large-scale industrial and mission-critical facilities. In this role, you will develop, coordinate, and maintain multidisciplinary BIM models across Civil, Electrical, Mechanical, Architectural, and Structural disciplines, enabling early design validation, constructability reviews, equipment planning, and cross-functional coordination.

You will partner closely with internal engineering teams, external design consultants, contractors, and project stakeholders to produce coordinated BIM deliverables that improve design quality, reduce project risk, and support efficient execution across Industrial Compute's global infrastructure portfolio.

Key Responsibilities:

 - Develop and maintain conceptual and schematic BIM models for large-scale industrial and MEP-intensive facilities.

 - Coordinate BIM models across Civil, Architectural, and Structural disciplines.

 - Create and maintain federated models used for design reviews, spatial coordination, constructability analysis, and clash detection.

 - Model major building systems including equipment layouts, utility corridors, electrical rooms, mechanical rooms, structural framing, site infrastructure, and architectural constraints.

 - Coordinate equipment clearances, maintenance access, routing zones, shafts, risers, utility entrances, and major MEP pathways.

 - Translate engineering sketches, basis-of-design documents, equipment lists, one-line diagrams, and planning documentation into coordinated BIM models.

 - Support early design activities including test-fit studies, routing evaluations, phasing plans, utility coordination, and design option analysis.

 - Maintain BIM standards including model organization, file naming conventions, worksets, shared coordinates, view templates, and model health.

 - Support multidisciplinary coordination using Navisworks, Autodesk Construction Cloud, BIM 360, Revizto, or similar collaboration platforms.

 - Prepare model views, coordination packages, exports, and documentation for design reviews and stakeholder meetings.

 - Support model-based quantity takeoffs, equipment tracking, asset information, room data, and design progress reporting.

 - Review consultant and contractor BIM deliverables for quality, coordination, completeness, and compliance with project BIM standards.

 - Help maintain digital design assets that support planning, design development, construction coordination, and operational handoff.

Discipline Focus Areas



CIVIL BIM DESIGNER

 - Develop site models including grading concepts, access roads, utility corridors, stormwater systems, underground duct banks, and civil infrastructure.

 - Coordinate civil infrastructure with building footprints, substations, generators, cooling equipment, underground utilities, and site constraints.

 - Experience with Civil 3D, ArcGIS, Revit Site, and utility modeling is preferred.


ARCHITECTURAL / STRUCTURAL BIM DESIGNER

 - Develop architectural and structural models including building shells, floor plans, slabs, structural steel, foundations, equipment pads, platforms, stairs, and access areas.

 - Coordinate architectural and structural constraints with MEP systems, utility entrances, equipment placement, and code-required clearances.

 - Experience with Revit Architecture, Revit Structure, AutoCAD, and Navisworks is preferred.

Qualifications

 - Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in Architecture, Engineering, Construction Management, Civil Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Structural Engineering, or a related technical field.

 - 3+ years of BIM modeling, BIM coordination, drafting, or design technology experience.

 - Experience developing 3D models using Revit, AutoCAD, Civil 3D, Navisworks, Inventor, SolidWorks, or comparable BIM/CAD platforms.

 - Experience supporting multidisciplinary coordination for complex industrial, infrastructure, or building projects.

 - Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, equipment layouts, design narratives, diagrams, and consultant deliverables.

 - Strong understanding of BIM standards, model organization, file management, and coordination workflows.

Preferred Skills

 - Experience supporting large-scale industrial, data center, manufacturing, utility, or other mission-critical infrastructure projects.

 - Experience developing conceptual and schematic design models in addition to construction documentation.

 - Strong understanding of multidisciplinary MEP coordination, equipment clearances, routing zones, and constructability considerations.

About the Team

OpenAI’s Legal team plays a crucial role in advancing our mission by tackling innovative and fundamental legal issues in AI. The team includes professionals with expertise spanning technology, AI, privacy, IP, corporate, employment, tax, regulatory, and litigation. If you’re passionate about meaningful and unique work as a technology lawyer, this team is for you.



About the Role

We are seeking an employment lawyer to help build the legal foundations for OpenAI’s next stage of growth. Working closely with our employment counsel team and colleagues across the company, you will shape practical approaches to challenging employment issues in a fast-growing AI company. This is a hands-on role for a thoughtful lawyer who enjoys variety, moves quickly, and wants to help build a strong employment legal function as the business scales.



You will collaborate with experienced employment counsel on US and international employment issues, the employment aspects of mergers and acquisitions, and emerging questions about AI in the workplace. A central part of your work will be turning lessons from individual matters into practical policies, guidance, and approaches that work at scale. You will also own stakeholder relationships and manage counseling matters, exercising sound judgment and taking responsibility for outcomes. You will join a bright, collaborative team that values initiative and shared learning, with opportunities to learn from senior colleagues, deepen your expertise, and take on increasingly complex matters over time.



This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.



In this role, you will:

 - Help shape OpenAI’s employment legal approach as the company scales, developing practical policies, playbooks, and processes that address recurring issues and support sound, timely decisions.

 - Collaborate with senior employment counsel and cross-functional partners on a broad range of US employment matters, including recruiting and hiring, performance management, employee conduct, leaves of absence, accommodations, and separations.

 -  Own designated stakeholder relationships and counseling matters, providing clear, practical advice and working independently while drawing on the team’s experience and judgment as appropriate.

 - Advise on international employment matters and support the employment aspects of mergers and acquisitions, including diligence and workforce integration, collaborating with local and specialist counsel as appropriate.

 -  Partner on strategic projects and emerging legal questions, including the use of AI in employment and workplace practices.

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced Data Center Electrical R&D Engineer to develop and validate next-generation power architectures for high-density AI infrastructure.

This role is focused on research, advanced design, modeling, prototyping, and technical validation rather than ongoing facility operations.  - Strong understanding of power-system modeling, short-circuit analysis, load flow, coordination studies, arc-flash analysis, power quality, grounding, and reliability.

 - Experience designing experiments, prototypes, pilots, or validation programs for new equipment or infrastructure technologies.

 - Experience directing engineering consultants, equipment manufacturers, and external technology partners.

title: Data Scientist, Cloud Distribution & Growth
description:
About the Team

Cloud service providers give developers a way to use OpenAI models in the environments where they already build and run software. Our team works with Go-to-Market (GTM), Product, Engineering, and Finance to understand which customers we can reach through these providers and what helps them grow from a first API call to a production workload.

About the Role

In your first few months, you’ll identify a customer segment or workload where OpenAI can grow, recommend an investment to GTM, Product, and Engineering, and define how we’ll know whether it brought new usage to OpenAI. Your first priority will be to explain what drives usage and revenue across providers. You’ll use that understanding to help GTM decide which customers and workloads to invest in and to build forecasts the team can plan against.

A customer might sign a substantial cloud commitment and send very little traffic. You can sit down with the account team, trace the customer’s first requests, and work out whether they need help launching, access to a different model, or more capacity. When you see the same opportunity across customers, your work can change where OpenAI invests.

In This Role, You Will:

 - Build a reliable view of the business from provider usage reports, billing records, and API logs. Show how new workloads, expansion, changes in price, and shifts in model mix contribute to growth.

 - Estimate how much demand cloud distribution adds to OpenAI. Trace customer activity across channels to distinguish new use cases from traffic that moved from the direct API.

 - Identify where customers are ready to scale. Combine what account teams hear with evidence on request failures, latency, and model availability. Work with Product and Engineering on a change and measure what happens to usage.

 - Shape growth plans with GTM and Finance. Estimate what existing workloads and upcoming launches can contribute by year end, test the assumptions that matter most, and recommend where to focus with each provider.

 - Own the consumption forecast. Compare forecasts with actual usage over the same period, explain the biggest misses, and use what you learn to improve the next forecast.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You:

 - Like questions that take you from a conversation with an account team to a query about a single API request. You’re curious about why a customer’s behavior differs from what the numbers first suggest.

 - Are comfortable making a recommendation while some questions are still open. You can tell a sales leader where you’d invest and explain to an engineer what evidence would change your mind.

Qualifications

 - Experience independently leading data science work on a product, growth, or commercial question that changed a business decision.

 - Strong SQL and Python skills. You can join incomplete datasets, choose the right unit of analysis, and validate an aggregate result against individual customers or workloads.

 - Experience using cohorts, experiments, or observational comparisons to assess what drove a change. You can explain how customer selection affects the conclusion and evaluate a forecast against a simple baseline.

Preferred Qualifications

 - Experience with API platforms, cloud marketplaces, enterprise GTM, or a usage-based business.

 - Experience connecting service reliability or capacity to customer adoption, or using demand forecasts to guide a commercial or infrastructure investment.

OpenAI, in close collaboration with our capital partners, is building the world's most advanced AI infrastructure ecosystem. The Industrial Compute organization develops and delivers the large-scale power, data center, and compute infrastructure required to support frontier AI systems. The Data Center Engineering team works across energy, electrical, mechanical, controls, site development, construction, commissioning, operations, and external partners to turn demanding campus power requirements into safe, reliable, and executable solutions.

About the Role

We are seeking a Design Engineer, Power Generation to develop and integrate power-generation systems for large-scale AI infrastructure campuses. You will translate campus load, reliability, schedule, and operating requirements into practical generation architectures and technical design criteria, supporting both behind-the-meter generation and hybrid grid-and-generation strategies.

This is an individual contributor role with broad technical ownership from early concept and technology evaluation through detailed design, equipment selection, construction support, commissioning, and performance validation. You will work with internal engineering teams, utilities, OEMs, EPC partners, developers, and operators to resolve interfaces, make disciplined tradeoffs, and establish repeatable power-generation designs that can scale across the portfolio.

Key Responsibilities

 - Develop power-generation concepts, reference architectures, design criteria, and site-specific requirements based on campus demand, phasing, reliability targets, grid availability, fuel strategy, site constraints, and operating objectives.

 - Evaluate generation technologies and system configurations, including gas turbines, reciprocating engines, fuel cells, battery energy storage, microgrids, black-start systems, and hybrid grid-connected solutions.

 - Define and review plant electrical and mechanical balance-of-plant requirements, protection and controls philosophy, grid-paralleling and islanding behavior, redundancy, maintainability, and operational modes.

 - Translate AI infrastructure load profiles and deployment schedules into generation capacity plans, equipment sizing, ramp strategies, performance requirements, and commissioning criteria.

 - Lead technical diligence of OEM, EPC, developer, and supplier proposals; review calculations, one-line diagrams, layouts, specifications, studies, schedules, and design assumptions to identify gaps and material risks.

 - Coordinate interfaces across utility interconnection, substations, campus electrical distribution, cooling systems, controls, fuel supply, emissions, water, civil design, permitting, construction, and operations.

 - Evaluate tradeoffs across availability, efficiency, emissions, cost, schedule, constructibility, scalability, maintainability, and long-term operating flexibility, and document clear technical recommendations.

 - Support equipment selection, procurement, design reviews, factory and site acceptance testing, construction issue resolution, commissioning, performance testing, and operational handoff.

 - Investigate design or field-performance issues, drive corrective actions with partners, and incorporate lessons learned into engineering standards, specifications, and future reference designs.

Qualifications

 - 8+ years of engineering experience in power generation or industrial power systems, including responsibility for generation facility design or integration.

 - A bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

 - Experience taking generation projects from concept and equipment selection through detailed design, with direct involvement in procurement, construction support, commissioning, or performance testing.

 - Strong understanding of generation technologies such as gas turbines or reciprocating engines and their supporting electrical, mechanical, and fuel systems, including protection, controls, grid paralleling, islanding, and black start.

 - Ability to evaluate engineering studies, drawings, specifications, and supplier proposals; identify technical risks; and make defensible tradeoffs among safety, reliability, cost, schedule, and maintainability.

 - Experience resolving design interfaces across engineering disciplines and coordinating equipment suppliers, engineering and construction partners, utilities, and operators.

 - Sound judgment around safety, reliability, constructibility, maintainability, and technical risk, with the ability to make decisions when requirements or information are incomplete.

 - Ability to document design requirements, assumptions, and decisions clearly and explain technical recommendations to engineering, delivery, commercial, and leadership teams.

Preferred Skills

 - Professional Engineer licensure and experience developing reusable engineering standards and reference designs across multiple projects.

 - Hands-on experience deploying and commissioning onsite generation for campuses or industrial facilities with demand in the hundreds of megawatts or more, including large load steps and rapid power fluctuations.

 - Experience co-designing and deploying battery energy storage systems (BESS) with onsite generation, including power and energy sizing, controls integration, load smoothing, and frequency support.

 - Familiarity with utility interconnection studies, emissions and environmental constraints, fuel-supply requirements, and generation permitting.

 - Experience validating generation and storage performance through dynamic studies and field testing, including load steps, load rejection, generator trips, and transitions between grid-connected and islanded operation.

 - Experience delivering phased campus power, including integrating temporary generation, permanent generation, storage, and utility service while maintaining power to operating loads.

You will write and debug software, run experiments against real workloads and hardware, and improve the tools and product used across engagements.

 - Own technical delivery for agreed semiconductor and AI-infrastructure workstreams, from initial scoping and prototypes through validation, production deployment and adoption.

We also draw on our investigations and in-depth analysis of a wide range of data sources to provide actionable quantitative and qualitative intelligence to OpenAI’s leadership.

I2 Engineering works hand in hand with I2’s analysts and investigators, building tools that expand what human experts can understand and accomplish. OpenAI's data center construction teams work with engineering, supply chain, safety, quality, commissioning and operations partners to deliver the infrastructure that supports our computing needs. title: Motion Designer
description:
About the Team

OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world.

This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning.

About the Role

OpenAI is seeking a Motion Designer to help tell the stories behind our research. You’ll translate complex ideas, emerging capabilities, and the work of our researchers into clear, engaging motion across films, launches, demos, and other communications.

Working within the creative team, you’ll partner with Research, Brand, and production teams to shape work from early concepts through final delivery. You’ll help determine what a story needs visually, explore different approaches, and bring those ideas to life through thoughtful design and animation.

This is a hands-on role for someone with strong motion craft, curiosity about unfamiliar subjects, and the ability to find a compelling visual approach when the brief is still taking shape. You’ll contribute to how OpenAI’s research is expressed in motion, developing original work and reusable approaches that help the team build on what it learns.

In this role, you will:

 - Develop motion concepts for research stories, working with creative partners and subject matter experts to understand the ideas and identify how best to communicate them.

 - Design and produce high-quality 2D and 3D motion for research films, launches, demos, and supporting content.

 - Apply and extend OpenAI’s visual and motion language, balancing consistency with the needs of each story.

 - Take work from visual exploration, storyboards, and animatics through animation, compositing, and final delivery.

 - Collaborate closely with designers, filmmakers, editors, producers, and researchers, bringing a motion perspective into the creative process early.

 - Translate technical or abstract concepts into visual sequences that are accessible to a broad audience while preserving the meaning of the underlying work.

 - Work with producers to scope projects, communicate dependencies, and maintain a high standard of craft as priorities and timelines evolve.

 - Present work clearly, explain creative decisions, and incorporate feedback from creative and technical partners.

 - Develop reusable assets, templates, and workflows where they improve quality and make recurring work easier to produce.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - 7+ years of experience in motion design across films, campaigns, launches, or other narrative work.

 - A strong portfolio demonstrating design judgment, animation craft, and the ability to carry an idea from concept through finished execution.

 - The ability to explore an open-ended brief, propose a clear creative direction, and refine it through collaboration.

 - Proficiency in After Effects and experience with Cinema 4D or comparable 3D tools, alongside editing and compositing workflows.

 - Comfort working in Figma and sharing work across design and production teams.

 - A strong understanding of typography, composition, timing, rhythm, and visual storytelling.

 - Experience making complex or unfamiliar subjects understandable through design and motion.

 - Experience working with subject matter experts and incorporating technical feedback without losing clarity or creative quality.

 - Curiosity about AI and research, and a willingness to learn enough about a subject to represent it thoughtfully.

title: Network Infrastructure Engineer, Global Network Infra (WAN)
description:
About the Team

OpenAI's Global Network Infrastructure team is responsible for building and operating the global network backbone that connects our rapidly expanding compute infrastructure. Our work enables reliable, high-performance connectivity across data centers, cloud service providers, and network points of presence (PoPs), supporting the infrastructure behind OpenAI's research and products.

As OpenAI continues to scale its compute footprint globally, we are expanding our network infrastructure to meet increasing demands for capacity, reliability, and operational efficiency. Our team works across physical network design, carrier connectivity, network deployment, and operational troubleshooting to deliver resilient infrastructure at exceptional scale.

About the Role

We are looking for a hands-on Network Infrastructure Engineer to help design, deploy, activate, and operate OpenAI's global wide area network (WAN) infrastructure.

In this role, you will take direct ownership of bringing new network connectivity online, working closely with fiber providers, cloud service providers, and internal infrastructure teams to establish reliable connectivity across our global backbone.

You will be involved in everything from physical network design and circuit provisioning to troubleshooting complex connectivity issues across Layer 1, Layer 2, and Layer 3. You will play a critical role in expanding our network footprint, bringing new PoPs online, and ensuring that our infrastructure operates reliably as OpenAI continues to grow.

We're looking for engineers who enjoy working close to the infrastructure, thrive on solving difficult networking problems, and bring an automation-first mindset to scaling network operations.

In This Role, You Will:

 - Design, deploy, and support WAN infrastructure across data centers, network PoPs, and cloud connectivity environments.

 - Own the end-to-end activation and turn-up of network circuits, working directly with fiber carriers and cloud service providers to establish and validate connectivity.

 - Troubleshoot complex network issues across physical, Layer 2, and Layer 3 infrastructure, including optical signal problems, FEC errors, routing issues, and connectivity failures.

 - Diagnose and isolate network failures across carrier, cloud provider, and internal infrastructure boundaries, driving issues through resolution.

 - Contribute to physical network infrastructure design, including port mappings, fiber and cable layouts, optical distribution frames (ODFs), and connectivity planning.

 - Monitor network health, circuit utilization, and performance to proactively identify capacity constraints and reliability risks.

 - Build automation and tooling to streamline network provisioning, deployment validation, troubleshooting, and operational workflows.

 - Collaborate with network engineering, data center infrastructure, and external service providers to support the expansion of OpenAI's global backbone.

 - Participate in an on-call rotation to maintain the reliability and availability of critical network infrastructure.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You:

 - Have hands-on experience deploying, activating, and troubleshooting WAN circuits with telecommunications carriers, fiber providers, or cloud service providers.

 - Have a strong understanding of networking fundamentals, including optical networking, Ethernet, TCP/IP, BGP, and Layer 2/3 connectivity.

 - Are comfortable debugging network issues across multiple layers, from physical fiber connectivity and optical errors to routing and traffic forwarding.

 - Have experience working with data center networking, carrier infrastructure, cloud interconnects, or large-scale WAN environments.

 - Understand physical network infrastructure concepts such as fiber cabling, port mappings, optical distribution frames, and network equipment connectivity.

 - Can independently investigate ambiguous connectivity problems, isolate root causes, and work across internal and external teams to restore service.

 - Have experience with scripting or automation tools and are motivated to reduce manual work through repeatable, scalable processes.

 - Enjoy working directly with infrastructure and take pride in owning technical problems from initial deployment through operational resolution.

 - Thrive in a fast-moving environment where infrastructure requirements evolve rapidly and engineering decisions have a direct impact on global scale.

Nice to Have

 - Experience building or operating large-scale backbone networks, hyperscale data center networks, or cloud provider interconnect infrastructure.

 - Familiarity with optical transport technologies, network telemetry, and advanced troubleshooting of physical network links.

 - Experience automating network operations using Python, Go, or infrastructure automation frameworks.

 - Experience deploying new network PoPs or supporting large-scale network expansion projects.

 - Experience collaborating with carriers, colocation providers, and cloud networking teams on complex connectivity deployments.

Why This Role Matters

OpenAI's ability to advance AI research and deliver products at global scale depends on reliable, high-performance infrastructure.

As a member of the Global Network Infrastructure team, you will help build the connectivity foundation supporting some of the world's most demanding compute environments. Your work will directly contribute to expanding OpenAI's global network footprint, bringing critical infrastructure online, and ensuring the reliability of the systems powering frontier AI.

This is an opportunity to work on challenging infrastructure problems, take meaningful ownership of global network deployments, and help shape the next generation of OpenAI's network backbone.

title: Product Cost Management Lead - AI Infrastructure
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization is building the infrastructure foundation for frontier AI systems. The Supply Chain organization enables scalable, resilient, and efficient supply chains across custom silicon, systems, networking, memory, storage, and rack-scale infrastructure.

Our team connects engineering, supplier strategy, manufacturing, planning, deployment, and finance to make hardware cost, supply, and execution tradeoffs clear from early architecture through production and sustaining operations.

About the Role

OpenAI is seeking a Product Cost Management Lead to own the official costed bill of materials (BOM), system and cluster cost and price baseline, and platform-to-platform total cost of ownership (TCO) for our 1P AI infrastructure. You will turn component, system, POD, manufacturing, deployment, DC, service, and lifecycle inputs into a trusted view of product economics that informs technical and business decisions, including transition timing.

You will partner with Engineering, Strategic Sourcing, Manufacturing-partner management, Finance, Planning, Supply Chain Program Management, Operations Program Management, and infrastructure teams to evaluate engineering / design changes, compare alternatives, identify cost-reduction opportunities, and track realized benefits.

This is an individual contributor role with broad cross-functional ownership. The ideal candidate combines hardware cost expertise, rigorous modeling, sound judgment, and the ability to explain complex tradeoffs clearly to engineering, operations, and senior leaders.

In this role, you will:

 - Own the official costed BOM and system/pod roll-up by platform, generation, configuration, build phase, volume, and mix. Maintain version control and traceability to quotes, source owners, assumptions, and engineering revisions.

 - Publish and maintain the system/pod cost and price baseline, reconciling component pricing and manufacturing-partner inputs with approved configurations and planning assumptions.

 - Build platform-to-platform TCO comparisons covering component content, non-recurring engineering, tooling, manufacturing labor and overhead, yield, scrap, test, logistics, deployment, housing and site costs, power and cooling, networking, spares, service, warranty, and lifecycle costs.

 - Partner with housing and site teams to integrate their cost inputs into product economics, documenting scope, timing, allocation assumptions, and gaps so platform comparisons are consistent and avoid double counting.

 - Quantify the cost impact of engineering change orders and notices (ECOs/ECNs), architecture, specification, configuration, and qualification changes before approval. Assess recurring and one-time costs, implementation timing, inventory exposure, and expected benefits.

 - Develop a prioritized cost-reduction, value-engineering, and second-source opportunity funnel with Engineering, Strategic Sourcing, and manufacturing-partner management. Evaluate qualification costs, investment, payback, supply improvements, and execution risk.

 - Analyze actual, forecast, quoted, committed, and purchase-price costs against the baseline. Explain material variances, identify root causes, and track recovery actions with accountable owners and dates.

 - Build sensitivity and scenario analyses for supplier and manufacturing-partner options, capacity, volume and mix, yield, configuration, site, deployment timing, and lifecycle tradeoffs. Present clear recommendations with assumptions, confidence ranges, and decision deadlines.

 - Validate savings and cost avoidance with Finance and accountable source owners. Distinguish identified opportunities, approved actions, and realized benefits, including offsets and implementation costs.

 - Establish cost-data definitions, BOM hierarchy, allocation methods, currency and volume assumptions, refresh expectations, and change-control processes. Flag stale, incomplete, or unsupported inputs before they affect decisions.

 - Lead recurring product-cost and TCO reviews. Publish concise cost bridges, opportunity updates, risks, and decision packages while retaining the supporting detail needed for technical and financial review.

 - Build scalable models, reporting, and data workflows that improve baseline completeness, refresh speed, analysis turnaround, and decision quality as the hardware portfolio grows.

 - You will own integrated product economics and the cost-analysis methodology and the cost analysis itself. Strategic Sourcing and manufacturing-partner management retain commercial negotiations; Engineering retains design and qualification authority; DC and site teams own their source inputs; Finance retains budgets, accounting, and financial approvals; Planning owns the demand baseline; SCPM owns material readiness; and OPM owns operational execution.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - Significant experience in hardware product costing, cost engineering, supply chain finance, manufacturing cost analysis, or a related role supporting complex technology products.

 - Experience building and maintaining multi-level costed BOMs, system cost roll-ups, and lifecycle or TCO models across product development, production ramp, and sustaining operations.

 - Strong understanding of hardware cost drivers, including component pricing, manufacturing labor and overhead, NRE, tooling, yield, scrap, test, logistics, and service costs.

 - Demonstrated ability to evaluate engineering changes, second-source options, and cost-reduction opportunities using comparable scenarios and transparent assumptions.

 - Advanced spreadsheet and quantitative modeling skills, with disciplined data reconciliation, version control, and source traceability.

 - Ability to turn incomplete or changing technical and commercial inputs into defensible analysis, identify uncertainty, and drive input gaps to closure.

 - Strong cross-functional influence and communication skills, including concise leadership recommendations and detailed working sessions with engineering, sourcing, manufacturing, and finance teams.

 - High ownership and sound judgment in a fast-moving environment with evolving requirements and competing priorities.

Preferred Qualifications

 - Experience with AI infrastructure, hyperscale data centers, custom silicon, servers, networking, storage, or rack-scale systems.

 - Experience analyzing JDM, CM, or ODM cost structures and open-book manufacturing models.

 - Familiarity with DC and site economics, power and cooling, deployment timing, spares, and service costs in infrastructure TCO.

 - Experience with ERP, MRP, and PLM systems, BOM change control, and business intelligence or automation/AI tools.

 - A background in engineering, finance, supply chain, manufacturing, or a related analytical discipline.

What Success Looks Like

 - Teams use a complete, current, and traceable costed BOM and system/pod baseline as the source of truth for product economics.

 - Platform TCO comparisons use consistent scope and assumptions, with inputs validated by their owners.

 - Material engineering and sourcing decisions include timely cost-impact analysis and explicit tradeoffs.

 - Cost variances have clear explanations, accountable owners, and recovery actions; savings and cost avoidance are validated.

 - Leadership receives clear recommendations, and cost-management processes scale with the complexity of the 1P hardware roadmap.

title: Research Engineer / Research Scientist, Human Flourishing
description:
About the Team

The Human Flourishing team’s mission is to ensure AI systems understand and advance human flourishing. As AI becomes more capable and plays a larger role in people’s lives, we want its human benefits to grow with its capabilities. The Human Flourishing team is part of the broader Personal AGI organization.

Our approach has two parts. Firstly, we measure and improve models’ understanding, capability, and propensity to act according to people’s values and to help them achieve their long-term goals. Secondly, we directly scale tangible impact for users in human domains like education and mental health, working across research, product, and partnerships to increase the benefits over a billion people experience weekly when they use ChatGPT.

Our recent work includes Beneficial RL https://alignment.openai.com/beneficial-rl/, which investigates how training for beneficial behavior generalizes across settings, and MentalHealthBench https://openai.com/index/introducing-mentalhealthbench/, a benchmark developed with mental health experts to evaluate realistic conversations.

About the Role

We’re looking for an exceptional, hands-on researcher to turn difficult-to-define signals of long-term flourishing into measurable improvements in model behavior. You’ll help set research direction, build what is needed to test your ideas, and drive successful work into the models and products we ship.

We’re especially interested in researchers with deep experience improving frontier models through pretraining or reinforcement learning (RL) / post-training, especially on less verifiable problems, or researchers who combine strong LLM skills with deep expertise in domains like education or mental health. Prior experience in these domains is not required.

In this role, you will

 - Develop scalable training methods across the training stack that improve how models understand people’s values, support their agency, and help them achieve long-term goals.

 - Lead high-leverage research from an open question to a shipped improvement: choose a hard-to-define problem, iteratively define success, run experiments, and integrate into frontier models.

 - Build RL environments for difficult-to-verify outcomes, and study whether beneficial behavior generalizes across settings.

 - Create evaluations grounded in human expertise and feedback that reveal capability gaps, unintended incentives in RL, and failures that aggregate scores can miss.

 - Test whether measures of model behavior predict better learning, wellbeing, and other long-term outcomes, and use those findings to guide training.

 - Build new 0→1 capabilities in human domains that may have an increasing impact with upcoming increases in model intelligence and test-time compute.

 - Partner with product teams, engineers, partnerships teams, and domain experts to deploy promising methods, measure their effects in real use, and turn what you learn into further improvements.

 - Assess AI’s impacts on human flourishing at the scale of over a billion users.

You might thrive in this role if you

 - Care deeply about helping AI improve people’s lives, and feel this is a responsibility that comes with increasingly capable models.

 - Have an unusually strong research record in pretraining or RL / post-training research, especially in a hard-to-verify area; or combine strong LLM research skills with deep expertise in education, mental health, or a related field of human benefit.

 - Are a hands-on builder who can turn ideas into rigorous experiments, write and debug code, and work directly with data and training infrastructure.

 - Have the taste to choose consequential problems and actionable steps on the path to solving those problems.

 - Take ownership of ambiguous problems and choose methods based on the impact they can deliver, including when the most useful work is unglamorous.

 - Care about whether a capability will scale, generalize, and make it into the real world—not just whether it can be shown in a paper or prototype.

 - Work well across disciplines and can grok the most important bottlenecks to scaling our impact in a multidisciplinary problem.

If you’re excited about ensuring AI systems advance human flourishing, we’d love to hear from you.

You should be able to move from complex external developments to clear decisions and requirements that teams can implement.

The team works across engineering and finance to make infrastructure spend visible, allocate capacity effectively, and improve efficiency as our products grow.

Our systems support the CPU, network, storage and GPU infrastructure behind products such as ChatGPT, the API, and Codex. We are expanding these foundations to connect resource usage, cost, forecasting, and planning so teams can make better decisions at scale.

 


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for a Software Engineer to lead the design, implementation, and operation of systems for infrastructure cost and efficiency. You will build the platforms that explain where infrastructure spend goes, identify opportunities to improve utilization, and help teams plan the capacity they need.

We ideally want direct experience building and operating software for infrastructure economics, such as usage metering, cost attribution, resource efficiency, budgeting, forecasting, or capacity planning. You should have owned systems that connect compute, storage, or network consumption to cost and help teams make measurable efficiency and investment decisions.

You will set technical direction for a growing area while staying close to the code. Working with infrastructure engineers, product teams, finance, and leadership, you will turn ambiguous business and engineering problems into reliable software, shared data, and measurable improvements. This role offers substantial autonomy and the opportunity to shape how OpenAI manages its infrastructure investment.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. This is an on-site role.
