title: Software Engineer, Traffic Infrastructure
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Cloud Infrastructure team builds and operates the infrastructure behind OpenAI’s products, including ChatGPT and the API. Within Cloud Infrastructure, the Traffic team owns how traffic enters our cloud environments, moves between services, clusters, and regions, and reaches external dependencies.

Our work spans cloud networking, Kubernetes networking, ingress and egress gateways, proxies, load balancing, and traffic steering. We build the systems, controls, and observability that make these paths reliable, secure, efficient, and straightforward for other engineering teams to use.

 


ABOUT THE ROLE

You’ll build and operate the networking and traffic infrastructure that connects OpenAI’s products and services across clouds and regions. The team’s work spans L3, L4, and L7—from IP connectivity, NAT, and transport behavior to service proxies and application request routing.

You’ll bring depth in part of this stack and curiosity about how the whole path works. Projects may include building gateways and control planes, improving cross-region connectivity, diagnosing packet loss or connection exhaustion, and making routing changes safer and easier to operate.

This role combines software engineering with production ownership. You’ll turn ambiguous networking problems into durable improvements, working closely with service owners, infrastructure teams, Security, and cloud providers.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA or Seattle, WA.

 


IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Design, build, and operate ingress, egress, and service-to-service connectivity across clusters, regions, and clouds.

 - Develop proxies, gateways, controllers, and automation for routing, load balancing, failover, and traffic management.

 - Build and evolve cloud networking infrastructure, including private connectivity, NAT, and network isolation.

 - Diagnose failures and performance bottlenecks across application, proxy, transport, and cloud networking layers; work with cloud providers when issues extend into their infrastructure.

 - Build telemetry and diagnostic tools that explain traffic paths, identify failing components, and help engineers take effective action.

 - Partner with Security to implement and validate traffic-path protections, including secure service communication, access controls, egress restrictions, and DDoS defenses.

 - Improve latency, throughput, availability, and network efficiency through measurement, testing, and careful production rollouts.

 - Create clear interfaces and safe defaults for service teams, participate in on-call, and turn operational lessons into changes that prevent recurring failures and reduce manual work.

 - Have 5+ years of experience building production infrastructure or distributed systems, including substantial work on networking or traffic infrastructure.

 - Have depth in one or more areas such as cloud networking, Kubernetes networking, proxies and gateways, service meshes, load balancing, or global traffic routing.

 - Understand networking fundamentals and can reason about how IP routing, TCP/UDP, DNS, NAT, TLS, and HTTP/gRPC affect connectivity and performance.

 - Have hands-on experience building or operating systems such as Envoy, NGINX, Istio, Cilium, or comparable networking infrastructure.

 - Write production software in Go, Rust, C++, Python, or a similar language, and use software and automation to solve operational problems.

 - Can investigate unfamiliar failures using evidence, test hypotheses, and follow problems through to a verified resolution.

 - Take ownership of design, implementation, rollout, and ongoing reliability, and communicate clearly across teams when a problem crosses ownership boundaries.

 - Care about making infrastructure secure and understandable for the engineers who depend on it.

Pipeline hygiene. Track pipeline quality in Salesforce and Clari across your districts. Follow up with AEs to update and clean opportunities, and flag hygiene gaps to the DM.

Cross-functional coordination. Act as the district’s day-to-day contact for Finance, Legal, Channel, Marketing, and SE teams on operational requests.

Forecast commits, deal strategy, AE coaching, and executive customer relationships stay with the District Manager.

Your DMs report more time spent coaching AEs and less time on operational work.

Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills. High familiarity with using AI to build dashboards, synthesize data, and increase operational efficiency.

Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.
What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.

Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. description: About Rivian Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. Role Summary We are seeking an IC Package Design Engineer to join our ASIC team. In this role, you will lead the physical layout, modeling, and analysis of advanced semiconductor packaging solutions for high-performance integrated circuits (ICs). You will collaborate closely with cross-functional teams, including IC Design, Signal/Power Integrity (SI/PI), PCB Layout, Mechanical, Thermal, and Test Engineering, as well as substrate vendors and OSAT partners to deliver robust, cost-effective packaging from concept through volume production. Responsibilities End-to-End Package Layout: Own physical layout execution, including die placement, bump assignment, floor planning, ball map optimization, bump-to-ball fan-out planning, stack-up definition, and layer planning. Advanced Packaging Implementations: Design and develop advanced IC packaging solutions, including flip-chip BGA (FCBGA), System-in-Package (SiP), and 2.5D/3D IC architectures (e.g., interposers, CoWoS, EMIB, FOWLP). Silicon, Package & Board Co-Design: Partner closely with silicon and system teams to align on die/package/PCB co-design, floor planning, ball map, and interposer routing. High-Speed & Power Delivery Network: define and route high speed interfaces (e.g., DDR, PCIe, SerDes), design robust Power Delivery Networks (PDN) with high di/dt requirement EDA Tooling: Create, manage, and validate complex package layouts using industry-standard EDA tools (e.g., Cadence APD/SiP, Cadence Virtuoso, Synopsys 3DICC, Siemens Xpedition). Verification & Signoff: Run Design Rule Checking (DRC), Layout vs. Schematic (LVS) checks, netlist verification, and strict Design for Manufacturing (DFM/DFT) reviews. Manufacturing Collateral: Generate and validate complete manufacturing collateral (Gerbers, ODB++, BOMs) for tapeout and manufacturing release. Multi-Disciplinary Convergence: Work directly with SI/PI, thermal, and mechanical engineering teams to achieve design convergence across power, signal integrity, thermal, and mechanical reliability constraints. Vendor & OSAT Integration: Interface with foundries, substrate vendors, and OSAT partners to evaluate design feasibility, select packaging materials and design rules, maximize manufacturing yield, and execute smooth tapeouts. Bring-up & Test Support: Assist in lab bring-up, debugging, and silicon validation for packaged devices; collaborate with test engineering teams on probe card and test socket interface design. Workflow Automation: Develop and implement scripting tools (e.g., Python, Tcl, Perl, MATLAB) to automate layout flows and enhance design efficiency. AI/ML Innovation: Explore and drive adoption of AI/ML-enabled methodologies (e.g., predictive analytics, layout optimization, automated rule checks) to scale productivity and decision-making. Qualifications Education: B.S. or M.S. in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field. Experience: 3+ years (5+ years preferred) of hands-on experience in semiconductor package and substrate layout design, particularly for high-speed (SerDes) and high di/dt IC applications. EDA Tools Proficiency: Proven expertise with industry-standard packaging EDA tools such as Cadence Allegro APD/SiP, Cadence Virtuoso, Synopsys 3DICC, Siemens Xpedition Package Designer, or Calibre/KLayout. Technical Fundamentals: Strong foundational knowledge of electromagnetics, impedance control, crosstalk minimization, substrate materials, thermal management, and mechanical reliability. Manufacturing Standards: Solid understanding of DFM/DFT principles, JEDEC standards, DRC/LVS signoff flows, and reliability qualification processes. Advanced Packaging Experience: Hands-on experience with heterogeneous integration, chiplet architectures, silicon interposers, and 2.5D/3D IC packaging technologies is preferred. Ecosystem & Vendor Track Record: A strong track record of working directly with top-tier OSATs, substrate manufacturers, and foundry packaging teams is preferred. Automation & Scripting: Experience writing scripts (Python, Tcl, Perl, MATLAB) for workflow automation or leveraging modern AI/ML applications within engineering workflows is preferred. Join Our Team as an Assembler!
Are you passionate about assembly? S&C Electric Company is seeking a dynamic individual to join our Vista & Vista SD Assembly team. As an Assembler, you’ll be crucial in ensuring smooth operations and supporting our diverse team. In this job, you will assemble VISTA units and corresponding subassemblies. You will work in a production environment, engage in continuous productive activity, and must meet requirements within time constraints. This is an assembly line operation involving as many as six stations. Initially you will be assigned to one station but will need to be flexible and open to working additional stations as business needs require. Tasks require a high degree of eye-hand coordination, manual dexterity, and the use of both hands and arms on a repetitive basis for a full range of motion. You will frequently use hand and power tools; occasionally work while standing on ladders; and occasionally work inside tight compartments.
Key Responsibilities:
Assemble VISTA Switch, both on the assembly line and directly on the shop floor.
Identify, transport, install, mount and bolt all types of components (ranging from 5 lbs. to 50 lbs., with assistance), including bus assemblies, high-voltage switches, mounting and support plates, lock assemblies,
Perform mechanical inspection using torque wrenches, screwdrivers, and tape measures.
Have proficiency in the use of simple material handling equipment, hand tools, power tools, simple gauges, instruments and overhead cranes.
Operate simple machinery such as automatic Press machines.
What you’ll Need To Succeed:
High School diploma / GED
Demonstrated knowledge of mechanical operations.
Demonstrated ability to use basic shop math and measurement tools such as tape measures.
Ability to follow standard work instructions, assembly drawings, and specifications.
Knowledge and ability to use air impact tools and other hand-held tools.
Preferred:
Previous experience in assembly or manufacturing is preferred.
Major Physical Demands:
Standing: Most tasks are performed in a standing position with intermittent walking.
Lifting: Frequent lifting of items ranging in weight from 5 lbs. to 50 lbs.
Walking: Occasional walking moderate distances (less than 1/8 mile).
Carrying: Frequent carrying of items ranging in weight from 5 lbs. to 25 lbs.
Pushing: Occasional use of electric hand truck to move parts a moderate distance.
Pulling: Occasional use of electric hand truck to move parts a moderate distance.
Bending: Frequent bending and crouching required to complete the assembly tasks.
Reaching: Continuous full range of motion from above the shoulders to below the knees.
Handling: Continuous handling of parts ranging in size from 5 lbs. to 25 lbs. along with a variety of hand tools.

title: Senior Staff Electrical Engineer (On-site)
description:
ABOUT STANDARD BOTS

At Standard Bots, we're revolutionizing real-world automation by making robotic systems accessible to everyone. Our AI-powered platform enables robots to tackle unprecedented challenges through an intuitive instruction interface, bringing the power of software automation to physical spaces.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

We're building Bolt, a mobile manipulation platform: an autonomous mobile base carrying our robot arms. We're looking for a Senior Staff Electrical Engineer to lead the hardware of that base, mechanical and electrical, from concept through a safety-certified fleet. You will set the hardware architecture, lead a team of mechanical and electrical engineers through prototype builds, test, and certification, and own the power system yourself: specifying and integrating the battery pack and charger from a battery manufacturer, and designing the high-current distribution, pre-charge and protection, safe power cutoff, and power delivery to drive motors, arms, and compute.


📍 LOCATION

This is an on-site role based at either our new Boston-area office or our Glen Cove, NY factory, where Bolt is designed, built, and tested, with some flexibility on days in the office once you're up to speed. On-site you'll build up a fully equipped electronics lab, a build area, a test floor, and the team steps from your desk.


RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Lead the Bolt hardware team of mechanical and electrical engineers: set the electrical architecture and work with the mechanical team to set the mechanical architecture, plan prototype builds and the test program, run design reviews, and drive decisions to closure with software, safety, manufacturing, and product

 - Own the hardware side of AMR safety certification with Functional Safety: the certification plan, the safety functions and their evidence, and the test-lab campaigns for ISO 3691-4, ANSI/RIA R15.08, and UL 3100

 - Contribute as an IC where your contributions can best be utilized

 - Specify, select, and integrate the battery pack, BMS, and charger from a battery manufacturer: requirements, vendor evaluation, BMS communication (CAN), charge and discharge limits, and pack-level safety and certification evidence

 - Drive key architecture and component decisions through requirements and trade studies (pack capacity, drive configuration, peak and regenerative current, thermal)

 - Do the hands-on, technically deep work: schematic capture, high-current PCB layout, board bring-up, test plans, and root-cause debugging on the bench and on the robot

 - Design for safety and certification: fault analysis, derating, and the power-cutoff paths that functional safety relies on (ISO 13849, IEC 62133 / UL 2271 at the pack interface, EMC)

 - Hire, mentor, and grow the hardware team, and be the primary technical contact for battery, charger, drive, and PCBA vendors


WHO YOU ARE

You've led the hardware of an AMR or comparable mobile robot from a blank page through safety certification and production, and you've designed and shipped its battery-powered systems yourself. You know the failure modes: inrush, regen on a full pack, ground loops, connector and busbar heating, a BMS that trips when you least expect it, and the safety function that fails validation a month before the audit. You can write a pack specification a vendor can build to and verify what they deliver. You lead by doing design work alongside the team. Our ideal candidate expects to spend roughly half their time on design/build/troubleshoot and half on team leadership, test, and certification.


SKILLS YOU'LL BRING

 - Experience: Bachelor's or graduate degree in Electrical Engineering (or related) and 10+ years designing, building, and testing power systems and PCBAs, including leading the hardware of an AMR, AGV, or similar mobile robot taken through production

 - AMR Safety Certification: You have taken an AMR or similar mobile machine through third-party safety certification (ISO 3691-4, ANSI/RIA R15.08, UL 3100), including ISO 13849 safety functions, the evidence package, and test-lab campaigns

 - Power Depth: Mastery of high-current distribution, pre-charge and protection circuits, DC/DC conversion, motor-drive power stages, and regen and bus-capacitance behavior

 - Battery Integration: Working knowledge of BMS behavior (balancing, SoC/SoH, protection limits, CAN interface) and how to specify, qualify, and integrate a vendor pack and charger

 - Compliance: Working knowledge of IEC 62133 / UL 2271 at the pack interface and EMC (IEC 61000 series) with pre-compliance debugging

 - Leadership: You have led engineers through an NPI cycle and made them better; you give direct, specific design feedback

 - Tool Fluency: Proficient in Altium Designer for schematic capture and multi-layer, high-current layout; LTspice or similar for simulation; Python for test automation

 - Debugging Mastery: Scope, current probe, thermal camera, and bench instruments; you document what you find and converge on a fix quickly

 - Clarity of Communication: Clear design documentation, crisp trade studies, and design reviews that make your peers better

 - Impact Driven: A reliable, manufacturable robot that ships beats an elegant one that never leaves the lab

 - Excelling in Ambitious Environments: You thrive in a fast-moving team with changing requirements and tight timelines


BONUS POINTS FOR

 - Mechanical design of mobile robots (chassis, drivetrain, battery packaging), enough to lead mechanical engineers well

 - Custom battery pack design (cell selection, pack mechanical and thermal design, BMS hardware)

 - Motor control (FOC, current sensing) and inverter design for traction or robot joints

 - Real-time industrial fieldbuses (EtherCAT, CAN/CANopen) and safety fieldbus

 - Taking products from prototype through NPI to volume manufacturing — DFM/DFT, test fixtures, yield improvement


COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

The base salary range for this role is $160,000 to $220,000, depending on experience. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. We also offer a package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees.

Data Engineering

Engineering Excellence & Collaboration

Tempus is on a mission to create the world’s largest integrated dataset of clinical and molecular data. As Senior Manager, Software Engineering, you will lead and mentor a small team of data engineers and data architects, and you will own the enterprise data model and the reliability of the data it represents. You will design how clinical records, genomics, next-generation sequencing (NGS) laboratory data, and radiology data are integrated, and you will ensure that the data are accurate, traceable, and suitable for critical applications such as machine learning and clinical decision-making.

Lead and mentor a small team of data engineers and data architects by conducting design and code reviews, providing technical guidance, and fostering a culture of excellence in data architecture and data quality.
Own and evolve an enterprise data model with engineers, product managers, scientists, and operators, integrating structured data from clinical records, genomics, the NGS laboratory, and radiology across relational and NoSQL data stores. Author and maintain entity-relationship diagrams, data dictionaries, API specifications, and data-translation documentation at the conceptual, logical, and physical levels.
Apply modern data architecture best practices and patterns, and teach modeling standards, including third normal form, dimensional (star schema) design, and established healthcare data model standards such as FHIR, OMOP, and related standards.
Evaluate the completeness of source-system models and partner data through profiling, and resolve structural inconsistencies before they reach downstream consumers.
Design observability for the data ecosystem with BigQuery, dbt, Elementary, and Grafana, including monitors, alerts, dashboards, lineage, and traceability back to source systems.
Partner with product managers and engineering leads to prioritize the backlog, estimate work, and translate complex requirements into actionable technical tasks. Advance the use of AI-assisted development, including Cursor, Claude, and GitHub Copilot, to accelerate modeling, testing, refactoring, and pipeline development.
Why We Are Looking for You
You have a record of leading and mentoring a small team of data engineers and data architects, of setting standards, and of guiding design in a fast-paced environment. You can translate gaps in the data model and in data quality into clear recommendations for engineers, scientists, and other stakeholders.
You are an expert in the modern data stack, particularly dbt, SQL, and Python, and you have demonstrated exceptional SQL skills in an enterprise data warehouse. You are proficient in the use of AI coding assistants such as Cursor, Claude, and GitHub Copilot.
You have applied modern data architecture best practices and patterns, and you can guide a team in their use. You have strong experience with third normal form (3NF) and dimensional (star schema) modeling; with established healthcare data model standards such as FHIR, OMOP, and related standards; and with modeling tools such as Erwin, Vertabelo, or Lucidchart.
You understand ETL/ELT and business intelligence (BI) architectures, and you can explain the long-term implications of choosing among relational, massively parallel processing (MPP), and NoSQL technologies. You have architected solutions across more than one of these technologies.
You have practical experience with data observability (for example, Elementary and Grafana) and with profiling and correlation analysis to identify data-integrity problems.
You have domain experience in healthcare and next-generation sequencing, including clinical and genomic data.
Preferred
Deep knowledge of Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and BigQuery architecture.
Experience modeling NGS data output.
Experience in implementing master data, reference data, or metadata management.
Why Join Tempus
You will work at the intersection of software engineering and cancer research. In this role, you will lead a small team of data engineers and data architects and shape the data model and quality systems that make Tempus data reliable enough for research and clinical use.

title: Field Merchandiser
description:
Job Family Group:
Retail Group
Job Description:
The Field Merchandiser is responsible for the hands-on execution of merchandising initiatives across TA locations. This position works as part of a traveling field team responsible for completing store resets, reflows, cooler resets and refreshes, remodel support, fixture changes, planogram implementation, promotional execution, backroom and storage organization, and other merchandising projects.
The Field Merchandiser may also assist with the reflow and remerchandising of deli and sales desk areas to improve product presentation, space utilization, customer experience, and operational efficiency.
This is a highly physical, hands-on role requiring frequent travel and the ability to work effectively in an active retail environment. Field Merchandisers will be expected to move merchandise, tear down and rebuild fixtures, stock and organize product, install merchandising materials, and ensure stores are completed according to approved layouts, planograms, merchandising standards, and BP safety requirements.
This role is 50 hours per week.
Key Responsibilities
Safety
Follow all BP and TA safety policies, procedures, and protocols at all times .
Complete required safety training and utilize required personal protective equipment (PPE).
Maintain a safe work environment for team members, store employees, customers, and vendors throughout each project.
Follow proper lifting, material-handling, ladder, equipment, cooler, and fixture-installation procedures.
Immediately identify and report unsafe conditions, damaged equipment, injuries, or other safety concerns.
Maintain clean and organized work areas during resets and leave stores safe and customer-ready at the completion of each workday.
Store Resets & Fixture Installation
Participate in complete and partial store resets, reflows, remodels, and merchandising refreshes.
Tear down, move, assemble, rebuild, level, and position retail fixtures and shelving according to approved store layouts.
Remove and reinstall shelves, peg hooks, displays, racks, endcaps, merchandising accessories, and other store fixtures.
Safely move product and fixtures throughout the store as required to complete resets.
Assist with receiving, staging, organizing, and installing new fixtures and merchandising materials.
Identify damaged or missing fixtures, components, or supplies and communicate issues quickly to the appropriate project leader.
Cooler Resets & Refreshes
Complete cooler resets, reflows, and merchandising refreshes according to approved layouts and planograms.
Remove, stage, organize, and replace refrigerated merchandise as necessary to complete cooler resets.
Adjust shelves, product placement, facings, and merchandising organization within coolers according to approved plans.
Assist with reorganizing cooler space to improve product presentation, shopability, inventory capacity, and replenishment.
Identify damaged shelving, fixtures, tags, signage, or other cooler-related merchandising issues and communicate them to project leadership.
Coordinate cooler work with store management to minimize product exposure and disruption to normal store operations.
Planogram & Layout Execution
Read, understand, and accurately execute approved store layouts, floor plans, planograms, cooler layouts, and merchandising instructions .
Set shelves, fixtures, products, and displays to the specifications provided.
Ensure correct product placement, facings, shelf heights, spacing, sequencing, and merchandising presentation.
Validate that completed sections match approved planograms and layouts.
Identify situations where store conditions prevent proper execution and call out those issues rather than making unauthorized changes.
Support field validation of new layouts and planograms and provide feedback when execution challenges are identified.
Backroom, Storage & Cooler Organization
Assist with the organization and improvement of backrooms, storage areas, coolers, and other inventory holding areas as part of store reset and reflow projects.
Organize inventory to improve accessibility, replenishment, inventory visibility, and overall store efficiency.
Help identify excess, obsolete, discontinued, damaged, or misplaced merchandise and follow established procedures for disposition.
Organize merchandising supplies, fixtures, shelving, signage, and other materials to improve store-level execution.
Help establish sustainable organization standards that store teams can maintain after the Field Merchandising team leaves.
Ensure backroom, storage, and cooler areas are left clean, organized, safe, and operationally functional.
Deli & Sales Desk Reflow Support
Assist with the reflow, reorganization, and remerchandising of deli and sales desk areas as directed by approved project plans.
Move and reposition merchandise, displays, shelving, racks, and other approved fixtures to support revised layouts.
Assist with improving product placement, customer flow, visibility, impulse merchandising, and overall presentation in these areas.
Support the merchandising of food, beverage, grab-and-go, impulse, and other approved products associated with deli and sales desk areas.
Install appropriate signage, shelf tags, promotional materials, and merchandising communication.
Work closely with store teams and appropriate functional partners to minimize disruption to deli, sales desk, and customer operations.
Product Merchandising
Remove product from existing fixtures and properly stage merchandise during resets.
Restock and merchandise products following completion of fixture, cooler, and Planogram work.
Identify discontinued, damaged, excess, misplaced, or non-planogrammed inventory and follow established procedures for disposition.
Ensure merchandise is properly faced, organized, priced, and presented before completing a project.
Install shelf tags, price labels, promotional signage, displays, endcap materials, and other merchandising communication.
Help ensure promotional and seasonal programs are implemented according to established standards.
Store & Team Support
Work collaboratively with store management and team members while minimizing disruption to customers and normal store operations.
Communicate project progress, execution issues, missing materials, inventory concerns, and other barriers to Field Merchandising leadership.
Assist store teams in understanding new layouts, cooler sets, merchandising standards, organization expectations, and other changes following a reset.
Maintain a professional attitude and represent BP/TA appropriately when interacting with store employees, customers, vendors, and other partners.
Support other field merchandising and retail execution initiatives as business needs require.
Physical Requirements
This position requires significant physical activity. Team members must be able to:
Regularly lift, carry, push, and pull merchandise, fixtures, shelving, equipment, and supplies.
Lift and move heavy objects, including items weighing up to 50 pounds independently , and heavier items with appropriate assistance or equipment.
Bend, kneel, squat, reach, climb, and work at varying heights throughout the workday.
Safely use ladders and approved material-handling equipment when required.
Stand and walk for extended periods, including the majority of a work shift.
Perform repetitive lifting, stocking, fixture assembly, cooler resets, and merchandising activities.
Work for reasonable periods in refrigerated cooler environments when completing cooler resets or organization.
Work safely in active retail environments that may include customers, deliveries, contractors, and ongoing store operations.
Reasonable accommodations will be considered in accordance with applicable law.
Travel & Scheduling Requirements
Frequent travel is required , including weekly and overnight travel.
Must be able to travel by automobile and commercial airline as business needs require.
Must be able to work at TA locations throughout the United States.
Must maintain scheduling flexibility based on project and store requirements.
Work schedules may include early mornings, evenings, overnight work, and occasional weekends depending on project needs.
Team members are expected to coordinate travel with other Field Merchandising team members when appropriate to improve efficiency and control travel costs.
Qualifications
Previous retail, merchandising, store operations, construction/fixture installation, warehouse, or related experience preferred.
Experience completing retail resets or working from planograms and store layouts strongly preferred.
Experience with cooler resets, inventory organization, or convenience/travel center merchandising is a plus.
Ability to read and accurately follow detailed instructions, layouts, diagrams, and planograms.
Strong attention to detail and commitment to execution standards.
Ability to perform physically demanding work safely and consistently.
Ability to work independently while also functioning effectively as part of a traveling team.
Strong communication and problem-solving skills.
Ability to adapt quickly when field conditions differ from plans while escalating decisions appropriately.
Valid driver's license and ability to meet applicable company travel requirements.
Measures of Success
Success in the Field Merchandiser role will be measured by:
Safety – Work is completed without compromising BP/TA safety standards.
Accuracy – Store layouts, cooler layouts, and planograms are executed correctly.
Quality – Fixtures, merchandise, pricing, signage, coolers, backrooms, and storage areas meet established standards.
Productivity – Projects are completed efficiently and within established timelines.
Consistency – Execution standards are maintained from location to location.
Organization – Backrooms, storage areas, coolers, and merchandising supplies are left organized and easier for store teams to manage.
Teamwork – Works effectively with fellow Field Merchandisers, store teams, and project leadership.
Cost Awareness – Uses company resources responsibly and coordinates travel and project activities efficiently.
Store Readiness – Locations are left clean, organized, safe, operationally functional, and ready to serve customers following completion of the work.
Role Expectations
The Field Merchandiser is expected to take ownership of execution. The role requires individuals who are willing to roll up their sleeves and physically complete the work , while maintaining high standards for safety, accuracy, speed, organization, and store presentation.
The scope of the role extends beyond simply resetting shelves. Field Merchandisers may work across the sales floor, coolers, backrooms, storage areas, deli, sales desk, and other customer-facing merchandising areas to help create a more effective overall store.
The objective is not simply to complete a reset. The objective is to leave each location safer, easier to shop, easier to replenish, better organized, easier for the store team to operate, and fully aligned with the approved merchandising strategy.

Discover your place with us and help our business meet the challenges of reimagining and reinventing the future of energy.
Lead Production Technician
ROLE SYNOPSIS:
The Lead Production Technician is a field-based technical leader who supports the Production Foreman by converting priorities into safe, reliable, and efficient field execution. This role serves as the primary technical resource and escalation point for Production Technicians and drives production uptime, troubleshooting, asset stewardship, and operational discipline across an assigned area.
KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES:
Own the day-to-day technical quality of field operations within the assigned area and ensure Production Technicians execute safely and consistently.
Serve as the primary technical resource and escalation point for Production Technicians.
Support startups, shutdowns, troubleshooting, and abnormal operations, providing on-site or remote technical support to resolve issues and stabilize production.
Escalate unresolved risks and issues to the Production Foreman with clear problem definition, field context, and a recommended path forward.
Train and mentor Production Technicians on proper use of PI Vision, CygNet, Ranger, and Power BI to identify deferring wells, trend production performance, and manage deferment priorities.
Review high-volume pads daily, monitor high-touch wells, and initiate corrective actions to support stable production.
Monitor gathering-system performance, alarms, and well behavior and coordinate actions on constraints.
Use PI Vision, CygNet, and Power BI to identify abnormal trends, underperformers, and downtime events before they escalate.
Evaluate high-spend project performance, including gas lift conversions, ESP installations, and base-well tie-ins.
Coordinate production recovery during midstream outages, weather events, and other high-impact or unplanned disruptions.
Manage deferment using Power BI tools, Code Manager, PI Vision, CygNet, and Ranger to maintain accurate production-loss tracking and prioritize the highest-impact items.
Partner with the Optimization team on deferment, well issues, and troubleshooting to drive production uplift and resolve chronic problems.
Align daily priorities with the Production Foreman and coordinate technicians, contractors, Maintenance, Automation, and Engineering resources.
Track work to completion, communicate remaining risks or open items, and use Ranger to direct technician efforts toward the highest-impact priorities.
Identify nesting opportunities to consolidate work, reduce mobilization costs, and improve field efficiency across technician routes.
Improve problem definition and maintenance-notification quality, support repairs, and verify issue resolution.
Identify repeat failures and collaborate with Production Engineering, Facilities Engineering, Artificial Lift Engineering, Automation, and Reliability teams on chronic equipment issues and active projects.
Lead by example in hazard recognition, safety observations, stop-work authority, and operational discipline.
Support SORAs, JSAs, permits, safeguard verification, pre-job meetings, housekeeping, and procedural compliance.
Hold safety conversations and complete safety observations during each rotation; ensure HSE compliance among field vendors and contractors.
Ensure technician routes are current on OOOOA inspections, site inspections, plunger inspections, and managed-valve registry requirements; address gaps and overdue items.
Validate well-coding accuracy for Normal Ops, Base Backout, and Engineering/Optimization and ensure technicians update coding daily to reflect real-time field conditions.
Confirm technician verifications are meaningful and identify non-repetitive gaps.
Lead operational handover of new pads from Commissioning to Production Operations and review performance, failures, and outstanding issues before acceptance.
Coordinate with Development to document events in Enbase from initial startup and perform initial operation and optimization following handover.
Participate in MOC reviews, PSSR walkdowns, PHAs, HAZOPs, and 30% design reviews.
Coordinate contractors and vendors in alignment with Operations priorities and verify work completion and safety compliance.
Coach Production Technicians, share lessons learned, maintain operating notes and shift handovers, and review technician night notes for completeness and repeat issues.
Maintain the Nauto KPI driving score, keep mileage and vehicle information current in the E-Fleet app, and complete scheduled vehicle maintenance.
Submit all travel and expense reports accurately and on time.
ESSENTIAL EXPERIENCE & EDUCATION:
High school diploma or equivalent required.
At least 5 years of direct production oil & gas experience
Demonstrated mechanical aptitude and troubleshooting skills.
Experience utilizing data and available resources to solve operational problems.
